name: Low End Theory
teaser: 1991 A Tribe Called Quest made jazz the backbone of hip-hop: upright bass, laid-back drums, and Q-Tip and Phife Dawg's traded verses. 'Scenario' and 'Check the Rhime' defined the Native Tongues sound. The album proved hip-hop could be both intellectual and funky.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to how the basslines carry every track — jazz bassist Ron Carter played on 'Verses from the Abstract'. The chemistry between Q-Tip and Phife is the album's engine.

name: Astral Weeks
teaser: 1968 Van Morrison's second album is a suite of stream-of-consciousness songs: 'Madame George', 'Cyprus Avenue', and the title track are jazz-folk meditations on Belfast and memory. Recorded in two sessions with jazz musicians, the album has no chord changes to speak of — just modal grooves. It is the most spiritual rock album of its era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the flow — the songs drift like memories, with bass and guitar circling the same themes. 'Madame George' builds to a climax of pure emotion.

name: Speaking in Tongues
teaser: 1983 Talking Heads' fifth album is their funkiest: 'Burning Down the House' and 'This Must Be the Place' are built on locked grooves and singable hooks. The tour was filmed for the concert movie Stop Making Sense. The album proved new wave could be a party.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the rhythm section — bassist Tina Weymouth and drummer Chris Frantz lock into grooves that make the songs irresistible. The album rewards dancing as much as listening.

tracks.title: This Must Be the Place (Naive Melody)

name: The White Album
teaser: 1968 The Beatles' double album is a sprawling document of a band pulling apart: 'Back in the U.S.S.R.', 'While My Guitar Gently Weeps', and 'Helter Skelter' show four solo careers in one record. The band recorded 30 songs in five months. The album is messy, brilliant, and endless.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the range — from the music-hall 'Honey Pie' to the metal of 'Helter Skelter'. Each member contributed songs written alone, making it a compilation of four voices.

tracks.title: The Continuing Story of Bungalow Bill
Why Don't We Do It in the Road?
Everybody's Got Something to Hide Except Me and My Monkey

name: The Great Twenty-Eight
teaser: 1982 Sun Records' compilation of Chuck Berry's first hits — 'Johnny B. Goode', 'Roll Over Beethoven', and 'Maybellene' — is the founding document of rock and roll. The songs are built on Berry's guitar riff and storytelling lyrics. Every rock band since has learned from them.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitar — Berry's signature riff opens nearly every song. The lyrics tell stories of cars, school, and teenage life with wit and rhythm.

tracks.title: I Want to Be Your Driver

name: Piano Man
teaser: 1973 Billy Joel's breakthrough album introduced his storytelling: 'Piano Man', 'Captain Jack', and 'The Entertainer' are songs about bars, dreams, and the music business. The title track is based on his own time playing piano in a Los Angeles bar. The album made him a star and defined his sound.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the lyrics — 'Piano Man' paints a bar full of characters, each with a verse. The accordion and harmonica give the album its saloon feel.

tracks.title: The Ballad of Billy the Kid
If I Only Had the Words (To Tell You)

name: The Wall
teaser: 1979 Pink Floyd's rock opera about isolation and madness: 'Another Brick in the Wall', 'Comfortably Numb', and 'Run Like Hell' tell the story of a rock star building a wall around himself. The album spent 15 weeks at number one and sold 30 million copies. It is the most theatrical album in rock history.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the narrative — the album is a continuous story with recurring themes. 'Comfortably Numb' features one of the greatest guitar solos ever recorded.

tracks.title: Another Brick in the Wall, Part 1
The Happiest Days of Our Lives
Another Brick in the Wall, Part 2
Another Brick in the Wall, Part 3

name: 3 Feet High and Rising
teaser: 1989 De La Soul's debut rebelled against rap's hardcore image with playful, eclectic sampling: 'Me Myself and I', 'The Magic Number', and 'Eye Know' sample everything from Steely Dan to schoolhouse records. The album's 'D.A.I.S.Y. Age' vibe made hip-hop whimsical for the first time. It remains a landmark of the Native Tongues movement.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the samples — the album was the first to use the phrase 'sampling' in its credits. The skits between songs frame it as a game show.

tracks.title: This Is a Recording 4 Living in a Fulltime Era (L.I.F.E.)

name: Paul's Boutique
teaser: 1989 The Beastie Boys' second album is a dense collage of hundreds of samples — from Beatles to public-domain recordings. 'Hey Ladies' and 'Shake Your Rump' are endlessly layered. The album flopped at release but became the template for sample-based hip-hop.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the samples — the Dust Brothers built the album from obscure records and sound effects. Each listen reveals new layers.

tracks.title: Looking Down the Barrel of a Gun

name: DAMN.
teaser: 2017 Kendrick Lamar's fourth album is a meditation on faith, sin, and fame: 'HUMBLE.', 'DNA.', and 'LOVE.' alternate between boasts and confessions. The album won the Pulitzer Prize for music — the first rap album to do so — and became the most-streamed rap album of its year.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the sequencing — the album is designed to be played both forward and backward, with each track leading into the next. The production by Mike WiLL Made-It and others is sharp and minimal.

name: Hunky Dory
teaser: 1971 David Bowie's fourth album is a songbook of characters and styles: 'Changes', 'Life on Mars?', and 'Oh! You Pretty Things' are glam-folk songs about change and identity. The album came a year before Ziggy Stardust and paved its way. It is Bowie at his most melodic.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the piano — Rick Wakeman plays on the album, adding a music-hall grandeur. 'Life on Mars?' was inspired by a Frank Sinatra song's failure.

name: Jagged Little Pill
teaser: 1995 Alanis Morissette's third album sold 33 million copies and made angry female voices mainstream: 'You Oughta Know', 'Ironic', and 'Hand in My Pocket' are raw and cathartic. The album won five Grammys including Album of the Year. It defined 1990s confessional pop-rock.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the dynamics — the album swings from whispered verses to full-throated choruses. 'You Oughta Know' was reportedly about a famous ex, adding to its edge.

tracks.title: You Oughta Know (Jimmy the Saint Blend) / Your House (a cappella)

name: Whatever People Say I Am, That's What I'm Not
teaser: 2006 Arctic Monkeys' debut was recorded after the band became famous through leaked demos on the internet: 'I Bet You Look Good on the Dancefloor', 'Fake Tales of San Francisco', and 'Mardy Bum' are sharp and funny. The album sold 360,000 copies in its first week, a UK record. It is the fastest-selling debut in British history.

exploreAction.targetName: Whatever People Say I Am, That's What I'm Not (2006) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the lyrics — Alex Turner writes about nights out with wry detail. The album's punk-funk sound was recorded live in the studio.

tracks.title: I Bet You Look Good on the Dancefloor
You Probably Couldn't See for the Lights but You Were Staring Straight at Me
Red Light Indicates Doors Are Secured
Perhaps Vampires Is a Bit Strong But...
From the Ritz to the Rubble

name: Achtung Baby
teaser: 1991 U2 reinvented themselves with industrial rhythms and ironic imagery: 'One', 'Mysterious Ways', and 'The Fly' are their most adventurous songs. The band recorded in Berlin's Hansa Studios, where Bowie made Low. The album sold 18 million copies and rescued the band from self-parody.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the textures — the Edge's guitar effects and the band's new electronic instruments. 'One' was written when the band nearly broke up; its lyrics are about reconciliation.

tracks.title: Even Better Than the Real Thing
Until the End of the World
Who's Gonna Ride Your Wild Horses
Tryin' to Throw Your Arms Around the World

name: The Nightfly
teaser: 1982 Donald Fagen's solo debut after Steely Dan is a concept album about growing up in the 1950s: 'I.G.Y.', 'New Frontier', and 'Maxine' are meticulous, warm, and literate. The album's production is among the best ever recorded. It remains a favorite of audiophiles.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album was recorded digitally with the finest musicians and equipment of the era. Every detail rewards headphones.

name: Amnesiac
teaser: 2001 Radiohead recorded Amnesiac in the same sessions as Kid A, but the songs are more song-like: 'Pyramid Song', 'You and Whose Army?', and 'Knives Out' are jazz, blues, and folk refracted through the band's anxiety. The album rewards the patient listener.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the piano — 'Pyramid Song' is built on a haunting figure inspired by jazz and classical music. The album's moods shift constantly.

tracks.title: Packt Like Sardines in a Crushd Tin Box

name: White Blood Cells
teaser: 2001 The White Stripes' third album stripped rock to drums, guitar, and a singer: 'Fell in Love with a Girl', 'Dead Leaves and the Dirty Ground', and 'Hotel Yorba' are raw and catchy. Recorded in four days, the album made the duo stars and kickstarted the garage rock revival.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the minimalism — Meg White's drumming and Jack White's guitar carry everything. The album's brevity and power made it a template for 2000s rock.

tracks.title: Dead Leaves and the Dirty Ground
I'm Finding It Harder to Be a Gentleman
Fell in Love with a Girl
The Same Boy You've Always Known
I Think I Smell a Rat

name: Life After Death
teaser: 1997 The Notorious B.I.G.'s double album was released two weeks after his murder: 'Hypnotize', 'Mo Money Mo Problems', and 'Sky's the Limit' are confident, funny, and dark. The album topped the charts for a month and sold 10 million copies. It is the definitive East Coast rap record.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the flow — Biggie's delivery is unhurried and precise. The album's skits and interludes frame it as a movie.

tracks.title: I Got a Story to Tell

name: The Blueprint 3
teaser: 2009 Jay-Z's eleventh album returned him to the top of rap: 'Empire State of Mind', 'Run This Town', and 'On to the Next One' are anthems of success. Alicia Keys sang the chorus of the lead single, which became his first number-one in a decade. The album proved the veteran could still dominate.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Kanye West and Timbaland contribute beats. 'Empire State of Mind' is the album's triumphant centerpiece.

name: Wonderwall
teaser: 1995 Oasis's second album (What's the Story) Morning Glory? made them the biggest band in Britain: 'Wonderwall', 'Don't Look Back in Anger', and 'Champagne Supernova' are singalong anthems. The album sold 22 million copies and defined Britpop. It also contains the most famous feud in rock: the Gallagher brothers.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the choruses — every song builds to a singalong moment. 'Wonderwall' was written by Noel Gallagher about his then-girlfriend.

tracks.title: I Am the Walrus (Live Glasgow Cathouse June 1994)

name: Voodoo People
teaser: 1994 The Prodigy's second album, Music for the Jilted Generation, fused rave, punk, and breakbeat: 'Voodoo People', 'No Good (Start the Dance)', and 'One Love' are aggressive and euphoric. The album sold 2 million copies and made rave music mainstream.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the beats — the album mixes breakbeats, hardcore rave, and punk guitars. The energy never lets up.

name: Axis: Bold as Love
teaser: 1967 Jimi Hendrix's second album is the psychedelic peak of his craft: 'Little Wing', 'Spanish Castle Magic', and 'If 6 Was 9' are built on his most inventive guitar playing. The title track's stereo panning was a studio landmark. The album is a bridge from the debut to his masterpiece.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitar — 'Little Wing' is a masterclass in chord melody. The album's mix was recreated from mono tapes after the stereo master was lost.

name: Let It Bleed
teaser: 1969 The Rolling Stones' response to Altamont and the end of the sixties: 'Gimme Shelter', 'You Can't Always Get What You Want', and the title track are dark, loose, and prophetic. Brian Jones's last session appears on two tracks. The album closes the sixties with a shrug.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the dread in 'Gimme Shelter' — Merry Clayton's wailing vocal was recorded in one take and nearly destroyed her voice. The album rewards loud speakers.

tracks.title: You Can't Always Get What You Want

name: Physical Graffiti
teaser: 1975 Led Zeppelin's double album is their most eclectic: 'Kashmir', 'Trampled Under Foot', and 'In My Time of Dying' move from heavy rock to funk to blues. The band recorded it over two years with leftover sessions. The album is the peak of their ambition.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Kashmir' — the orchestra and guitar create a sound unlike anything else in their catalog. The album rewards a full, loud listen.

name: Loaded
teaser: 1970 The Velvet Underground's fourth album, named to satisfy a commercial push, is their most accessible: 'Sweet Jane', 'Rock & Roll', and 'Who Loves the Sun' are pop songs with an edge. Lou Reed wrote them to be hits; they became the band's most covered songs.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the pop craft — 'Sweet Jane' has the band's most singable riff. The album proves the Velvets could write hooks when they wanted.

name: Transformer
teaser: 1972 Lou Reed's second solo album, produced by David Bowie and Mick Ronson, turned his street poetry into glam rock: 'Walk on the Wild Side', 'Perfect Day', and 'Satellite of Love' are literate and catchy. The album made Reed a star without softening him.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to Ronson's arrangements — the strings and piano give the album its elegance. 'Walk on the Wild Side' became his signature due to its bassline and chorus.

name: Berlin
teaser: 1973 Lou Reed's third solo album is a harrowing concept record about addiction and abuse: 'Caroline Says', 'The Bed', and 'Oh, Jim' are brutal and beautiful. Producer Bob Ezrin built a cinematic wall of sound. The album flopped at release; it is now regarded as Reed's most ambitious work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the narrative — the album tells a continuous story from start to finish. The orchestral arrangements contrast with the bleakness of the lyrics.

tracks.title: How Do You Think It Feels

name: Songs from the Big Chair
teaser: 1985 Tears for Fears' second album made synth-pop stadium-sized: 'Everybody Wants to Rule the World', 'Shout', and 'Head over Heels' are anthems about psychology and power. The album sold 10 million copies and defined mid-80s pop. The band's therapy-inspired lyrics gave the music depth.

exploreAction.targetName: Songs from the Big Chair (1985) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album layers synthesizers, guitars, and a full band into a massive sound. 'Shout' was written about primal therapy.

tracks.title: Everybody Wants to Rule the World

name: Brothers in Arms
teaser: 1985 Dire Straits' fifth album was the first million-selling CD: 'Money for Nothing', 'Walk of Life', and 'Brothers in Arms' are polished and melancholy. Mark Knopfler's guitar and the album's digital recording made it a showcase for the new format. It sold 30 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitar tones — the album was one of the first recorded digitally, and the sound is pristine. 'Money for Nothing' was written in a store watching MTV.

name: So
teaser: 1986 Peter Gabriel's fifth album is his pop breakthrough: 'Sledgehammer', 'In Your Eyes', and 'Don't Give Up' with Kate Bush are cinematic and warm. The album's video for 'Sledgehammer' won nine MTV awards. It sold 5 million copies and made Gabriel a star.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Daniel Lanois gave the album its airy, spacious sound. 'In Your Eyes' became a wedding staple after being featured in a famous film scene.

name: The Immaculate Collection
teaser: 1990 Madonna's greatest-hits compilation is a decade of reinvention in one disc: 'Vogue', 'Like a Prayer', and 'Material Girl' trace her transformation from dance-pop to icon. The album sold 30 million copies. It remains the best-selling compilation by a solo artist.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the remixes — several tracks were re-recorded or remixed for the collection. 'Vogue' introduced house music to the mainstream.

name: Faith
teaser: 1987 George Michael's solo debut mixed pop, soul, and gospel: 'Faith', 'Father Figure', and 'One More Try' are confident and intimate. The album sold 25 million copies and won Album of the Year at the Grammys. It made him one of the decade's biggest stars.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album was recorded in his home studio with multiple instruments played by Michael himself. The title track's stomp is iconic.

name: Appetite for Destruction
teaser: 1987 Guns N' Roses' debut sold 30 million copies and defined late-80s hard rock: 'Welcome to the Jungle', 'Paradise City', and 'Sweet Child o' Mine' are sleazy, dangerous, and catchy. The band's chemistry made them the biggest rock act of the decade's end.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the interplay between Slash's guitar and Axl Rose's vocals — the album is a masterclass in rock dynamics. The cover art caused controversy on release.

name: And Justice for All
teaser: 1988 Metallica's fourth album is their most complex: 'One', 'Blackened', and the title track are technical and relentless. The production famously buried the bass, a source of fan debate for decades. The album is a bridge from thrash to mainstream metal.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the riffs — the album is built on intricate, changing time signatures. 'One' was inspired by the anti-war film Johnny Got His Gun.

name: Metallica
teaser: 1991 Metallica's self-titled 'Black Album' made heavy metal stadium-sized: 'Enter Sandman', 'Nothing Else Matters', and 'Sad but True' are slower, heavier, and more melodic. Produced by Bob Rock, the album sold 30 million copies. It is the best-selling metal album of all time.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Bob Rock pushed the band to simplify and tighten their songs. The album's sound is bigger and cleaner than anything before it.

name: Chronicle
teaser: 1976 Creedence Clearwater Revival's greatest hits compile their run of 1960s and early-70s classics: 'Fortunate Son', 'Proud Mary', and 'Bad Moon Rising' are protest songs and swamp rock. The compilation sold 8 million copies. It is the definitive CCR document.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the songwriting — John Fogerty wrote and produced nearly everything. 'Fortunate Son' remains the definitive anti-war protest song of its era.

tracks.title: I Put a Spell on You
Long As I Can See the Light
I Heard It Through the Grapevine
Have You Ever Seen the Rain?

name: Hot Rats
teaser: 1969 Frank Zappa's second solo album is a jazz-rock instrumental masterpiece: 'Peaches en Regalia', 'Willie the Pimp', and 'The Gumbo Variations' showcase his guitar and composition. The album features Captain Beefheart's only vocals. It is Zappa's most accessible work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the arrangements — the album is a fusion of jazz, rock, and classical forms. 'Peaches en Regalia' became Zappa's signature tune.

name: Over-Nite Sensation
teaser: 1973 Frank Zappa's breakthrough album blends jazz fusion with comedic lyrics: 'Dinah-Moe Humm', 'Camarillo Brillo', and 'I'm the Slime' are tight, dirty, and virtuosic. The album made Zappa a star with the mainstream. Its production is among his cleanest.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the band — the album's lineup includes future stars like Jean-Luc Ponty and Ruth Underwood. The horn and percussion arrangements are flawless.

name: Apostrophe
teaser: 1974 Frank Zappa's highest-charting album: 'Don't Eat the Yellow Snow', 'Cosmik Debris', and the title track are surreal, funky, and funny. The album's concept follows a boy's adventures in the snow. It reached number 10 on the Billboard chart.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the bass — Jack Bruce of Cream plays on the title track. The album's humor is inseparable from its musical sophistication.

name: Joe's Garage
teaser: 1979 Frank Zappa's rock opera about the dangers of music: 'Joe's Garage', 'Watermelon in Easter Hay', and 'Central Scrutinizer' tell the story of a musician in a world where music is illegal. The three-act structure is his most ambitious narrative. The guitar solos are among his best.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the story — the album follows Joe from garage rocker to prisoner. The guitar solo in 'Watermelon in Easter Hay' is Zappa's most emotional.

tracks.title: Why Does It Hurt When I Pee?
Lucille Has Messed My Mind Up
He Used to Cut the Grass

name: In the Court of the Crimson King
teaser: 1969 King Crimson's debut invented progressive rock: '21st Century Schizoid Man', 'Epitaph', and the title track are dark, symphonic, and apocalyptic. The album's Mellotron and jazz-influenced drums defined the genre. It is one of the most influential rock debuts ever.

exploreAction.targetName: In the Court of the Crimson King (1969) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the Mellotron — the keyboard's choir and string sounds give the album its eerie grandeur. '21st Century Schizoid Man' is proto-metal.

tracks.title: The Court of the Crimson King

name: Close to the Edge
teaser: 1972 Yes's fifth album is progressive rock at its most ambitious: the 18-minute title track, 'And You and I', and 'Siberian Khatru' are intricate and majestic. The band's virtuosity and Jon Anderson's ethereal vocals define the genre. It is the definitive prog album.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the structure — the title track is one continuous piece with recurring themes. The album rewards focused listening.

tracks.title: And You and I / I. "Cord of Life (3:46) / II. "Eclipse (2:30) / III. "The Preacher, the Teacher (3:10) / IV. "The Apocalypse

name: Fragile
teaser: 1971 Yes's fourth album features each member's solo piece alongside the band's epics: 'Roundabout', 'South Side of the Sky', and 'Heart of the Sunrise' are virtuosic and melodic. Rick Wakeman's keyboards added a new dimension. The album was their international breakthrough.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Roundabout' — its opening bass and guitar riff is one of the most recognizable in prog. The album rewards headphones for its intricate layering.

name: The Yes Album
teaser: 1971 Yes's third album marked their turn to progressive rock: 'Yours Is No Disgrace', 'Starship Trooper', and 'I've Seen All Good People' are long, intricate, and melodic. Steve Howe's guitar became the band's signature voice. The album is their first masterpiece.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the arrangements — the band moves between folk, jazz, and rock within single songs. 'Starship Trooper' has one of Howe's best guitar solos.

name: Moving Pictures
teaser: 1981 Rush's eighth album is their commercial peak: 'Tom Sawyer', 'Limelight', and 'YYZ' are tight, virtuosic, and catchy. The band's prog-metal sound reached its most accessible form. The album is a gateway into Rush's massive catalog.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the interplay — Geddy Lee's bass, Alex Lifeson's guitar, and Neil Peart's drums lock into intricate grooves. 'YYZ' is named after Toronto's airport code.

teaser: 1976 Rush's fourth album's side-long title track tells the story of a future where music is forbidden: 'Overture', 'The Temples of Syrinx', and 'Grand Finale' are sci-fi rock theater. Side two's shorter songs balanced the epic. The album saved the band's career.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the story — the title suite is a complete narrative inspired by Ayn Rand's ideas. The band fought their label to release it as the A-side.

name: Hemispheres
teaser: 1978 Rush's sixth album continued their sci-fi saga: 'Cygnus X-1 Book II' and 'La Villa Strangiato' are long, complex, and epic. The band's virtuosity is on full display. The album is the climax of their prog period.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'La Villa Strangiato' — an instrumental that moves through multiple moods and styles. The band considered it their most difficult piece to play.

name: Permanent Waves
teaser: 1980 Rush's seventh album trimmed their epics into tighter songs: 'The Spirit of Radio', 'Freewill', and 'Jacob's Ladder' are progressive but accessible. The album marked the band's shift toward shorter, hookier material. It reached number four on the Billboard chart.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'The Spirit of Radio' — its reggae section and jazz outro show the band's range. The album is a bridge between their prog and synth eras.

name: A Farewell to Kings
teaser: 1977 Rush's fifth album blended their prog epics with the emerging new wave: 'Closer to the Heart', 'Xanadu', and the title track are grand and melodic. The band recorded it in Wales with a classical guitarist on loan. The album expands their sonic palette.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the acoustic textures — classical guitar appears throughout the album. 'Xanadu' is one of their most ambitious epics.

tracks.title: Cygnus X-1 Book I: The Voyage :"Prologue (5:01) :"1 (0:44) :"2 (1:30) :"3

name: Gaucho
teaser: 1980 Steely Dan's seventh album took five years and cost over a million dollars: 'Hey Nineteen', 'Time Out of Mind', and the title track are sleek, sardonic, and immaculate. The band broke up after its release, exhausted by perfectionism. It is their most polished work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album's sound is a benchmark of studio craft. 'Time Out of Mind' features a sax solo by Mark Knopfler.

name: Pretzel Logic
teaser: 1974 Steely Dan's third album is their most varied: 'Rikki Don't Lose That Number', 'Any Major Dude Will Tell You', and the title track mix jazz, rock, and pop. The band's writing duo, Becker and Fagen, were moving away from live performance toward studio perfection. The album reached number eight.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the songcraft — every track is immaculate. 'Rikki Don't Lose That Number' was inspired by a Horace Silver jazz lick.

tracks.title: Any Major Dude Will Tell You

name: Can't Buy a Thrill
teaser: 1972 Steely Dan's debut introduced their literate jazz-rock: 'Do It Again', 'Reelin' in the Years', and 'Dirty Work' are sly, polished, and catchy. The band's anonymous studio approach set the template for their career. The album made them stars.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitar — 'Reelin' in the Years' features one of the most famous solos in rock. The album's debut was under a band name that was also a pseudonym.

tracks.title: Only a Fool Would Say That

name: Countdown to Ecstasy
teaser: 1973 Steely Dan's second album is darker and more complex than the debut: 'My Old School', 'Bodhisattva', and 'Show Biz Kids' are sardonic and funky. The band's growing perfectionism shows in every arrangement. It is a bridge to their masterpiece era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the funk — 'Bodhisattva' is the band's most driving track. The lyrics are among Becker and Fagen's most oblique.

name: The Royal Scam
teaser: 1976 Steely Dan's fifth album is their most guitar-driven: 'Kid Charlemagne', 'The Caves of Altamira', and 'Haitian Divorce' are funky, cinematic, and sardonic. Larry Carlton's solos are among the best on any Dan record. The album is a high point of their 70s run.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitar solos — Larry Carlton played many of them in single takes. 'Kid Charlemagne' was written about a fictional LSD chemist.

name: Bad
teaser: 1987 Michael Jackson's follow-up to Thriller was a worldwide smash: 'Bad', 'The Way You Make Me Feel', and 'Smooth Criminal' are sleek and confident. The album produced five number-one singles, a record. Its title track's music video with Martin Scorsese was a landmark.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Quincy Jones and Jackson crafted a harder, more aggressive sound. 'Smooth Criminal' features one of Jackson's most iconic dance routines.

tracks.title: The Way You Make Me Feel
I Just Can't Stop Loving You

name: Dangerous
teaser: 1991 Michael Jackson's eighth album blended new jack swing, funk, and rock: 'Black or White', 'Remember the Time', and 'Jam' are political and danceable. The album's 13-minute 'Black or White' video premiered worldwide. It sold 30 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Teddy Riley's new jack swing gave the album a modern edge. The album's social themes were a shift from his earlier work.

tracks.title: Why You Wanna Trip on Me

name: Ray of Light
teaser: 1998 Madonna's seventh album turned her toward electronic and spiritual themes: 'Frozen', 'Ray of Light', and 'The Power of Good-Bye' are ambient and danceable. Produced with William Orbit, the album won four Grammys. It is her most acclaimed work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Orbit's electronic textures give the album its otherworldly atmosphere. 'Ray of Light' was a reinvention that kept her at pop's forefront.

tracks.title: To Have and Not to Hold

name: True Blue
teaser: 1986 Madonna's third album is a pop landmark: 'Live to Tell', 'Papa Don't Preach', and 'Open Your Heart' are confident and catchy. The album sold 25 million copies and produced four number-one singles. It is the peak of her 80s pop era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the hooks — every track is built for the radio. 'Papa Don't Preach' sparked controversy for its topic of teen pregnancy.

tracks.title: Love Makes the World Go Round

name: American Life
teaser: 2003 Madonna's ninth album is her most political and divisive: 'American Life', 'Hollywood', and 'Die Another Day' critique American culture with electronic folk. The album's title track video was pulled after controversy. It is her most underrated record.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the lyrics — the album is a critique of celebrity and consumer culture. The acoustic guitars mixed with electronic beats were ahead of their time.

name: Music
teaser: 2000 Madonna's eighth album embraced European dance music: 'Music', 'Don't Tell Me', and 'What It Feels Like for a Girl' are sleek and futuristic. Produced with Mirwais, the album gave her a new electronic sound. It sold 11 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Mirwais's filtered beats and glitch effects were cutting-edge. 'Music' became a global dance anthem.

tracks.title: What It Feels Like for a Girl

teaser: 2011 Beyoncé's fourth album stripped her sound back to soul and funk: 'Run the World (Girls)', 'Love on Top', and 'Countdown' are confident and playful. The album's vocal runs and horns reference 80s R&B. It is a fan favorite in her catalog.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album mixes live instrumentation with electronic beats. 'Countdown' samples Boyz II Men and was inspired by reggae.

name: Dangerously in Love
teaser: 2003 Beyoncé's solo debut established her as a superstar apart from Destiny's Child: 'Crazy in Love', 'Baby Boy', and 'Me, Myself and I' are confident and catchy. The album sold 11 million copies and won five Grammys. 'Crazy in Love' remains her signature.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Crazy in Love' — its horn sample and drum break made it an instant classic. The album blends R&B, pop, and reggae.

tracks.title: The Closer I Get to You

name: Tidal
teaser: 1996 Fiona Apple's debut won a Grammy for Best Rock Vocal: 'Shadowboxer', 'Criminal', and 'Sleep to Dream' are dark, jazzy, and precociously mature. The album's confessional lyrics and piano-driven sound made her a star at 19. It sold 2 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the piano — Apple's playing is percussive and jazz-influenced. The video for 'Criminal' sparked controversy and fame.

name: Butterfly
teaser: 1997 Mariah Carey's sixth album blended hip-hop with her signature ballads: 'Honey', 'Butterfly', and 'My All' are sleek and personal. The album marked her artistic reinvention after her divorce. It is her most critically acclaimed work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album features collaborations with hip-hop producers like Puff Daddy. 'Honey' introduced a more urban sound to her catalog.

name: The Emancipation of Mimi
teaser: 2005 Mariah Carey's comeback album re-established her as a chart force: 'We Belong Together', 'Shake It Off', and 'Don't Forget About Us' are sleek R&B anthems. The album sold 10 million copies and produced two number-one singles. It is her best-selling album of the 2000s.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album blends hip-hop beats with her vocal gymnastics. 'We Belong Together' was the decade's biggest R&B hit.

tracks.title: Makin' It Last All Night (What It Do)
So Lonely (One and Only Part II)

name: Daydream
teaser: 1995 Mariah Carey's fifth album is her most seamless fusion of pop and R&B: 'Fantasy', 'One Sweet Day', and 'Always Be My Baby' are smooth and effortless. The album sold 20 million copies and produced two number-one singles. It is her commercial peak.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the vocals — the album showcases her five-octave range. 'Fantasy' was the first song by a female artist to debut at number one.

name: Music Box
teaser: 1993 Mariah Carey's third album made her a global superstar: 'Dreamlover', 'Hero', and 'Without You' are ballads and dance-pop at their most polished. The album sold 28 million copies. It remains one of the best-selling albums of all time.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the ballads — 'Hero' became an anthem of personal strength. The album's production is immaculate mid-90s pop.

tracks.title: Just to Hold You Once Again

name: The Bodyguard
teaser: 1992 Whitney Houston's soundtrack album is the best-selling soundtrack of all time: 'I Will Always Love You', 'I Have Nothing', and 'Run to You' showcase her voice at its peak. The album sold 45 million copies. Dolly Parton's song became Houston's signature.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'I Will Always Love You' — the a cappella opening builds into one of the greatest vocal performances ever recorded. The album won Album of the Year at the Grammys.

tracks.title: Even If My Heart Would Break
It's Gonna Be a Lovely Day
(What's So Funny 'Bout) Peace, Love, and Understanding

name: Whitney
teaser: 1987 Whitney Houston's second album made her the first woman to debut at number one: 'I Wanna Dance with Somebody', 'Didn't We Almost Have It All', and 'So Emotional' are pop-soul anthems. The album sold 20 million copies and produced four number-one singles.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Narada Michael Walden's arrangements gave the album its polished sound. The album cemented Houston as the decade's biggest female star.

tracks.title: Saving All My Love for You
Nobody Loves Me Like You Do
Take Good Care of My Heart

name: Whitney Houston
teaser: 1985 Whitney Houston's debut made her an overnight star: 'Saving All My Love for You', 'How Will I Know', and 'Greatest Love of All' showcase her voice and elegance. The album sold 25 million copies and produced three number-one singles. It is one of the best-selling debuts ever.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the range — the album displays her gospel-trained voice across pop, R&B, and ballads. 'Greatest Love of All' became an anthem of self-esteem.

tracks.title: Saving All My Love for You
Nobody Loves Me Like You Do
Take Good Care of My Heart

name: I'm Your Baby Tonight
teaser: 1990 Whitney Houston's third album embraced new jack swing: 'I'm Your Baby Tonight', 'All the Man That I Need', and 'Miracle' are sleek and confident. The album sold 10 million copies and produced three number-one singles. It modernized her sound for the new decade.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — L.A. Reid and Babyface gave the album a contemporary R&B edge. The title track is a new jack swing showcase.

tracks.title: All the Man That I Need

teaser: 2015 Adele's third album addressed motherhood and maturity: 'Hello', 'When We Were Young', and 'Send My Love (To Your New Lover)' are polished and emotional. The album sold 22 million copies and won Album of the Year. 'Hello' broke streaming records on release.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Greg Kurstin and Max Martin crafted a more restrained sound. 'Hello' was written about reaching out to people from the past.

tracks.title: Send My Love (To Your New Lover)

teaser: 2008 Adele's debut introduced her voice to the world: 'Chasing Pavements', 'Hometown Glory', and 'Make You Feel My Love' are folk and soul ballads. The album won a Grammy for Best New Artist. It sold 9 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the restraint — the debut is simpler than her later work, letting her voice carry the songs. 'Hometown Glory' was written about London at 18.

tracks.title: That’s It, I Quit, I'm Moving On

name: The Fame
teaser: 2008 Lady Gaga's debut made electro-pop a movement: 'Just Dance', 'Poker Face', and 'Paparazzi' are hook-filled and theatrical. The album sold 15 million copies and won a Grammy. It introduced her as pop's most ambitious new star.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — RedOne's beats gave the album its dance-floor energy. 'Poker Face' was a global number one and remains her signature.

tracks.title: Eh, Eh (Nothing Else I Can Say)

name: Born This Way
teaser: 2011 Lady Gaga's second album is a maximalist statement of self-acceptance: 'Born This Way', 'Judas', and 'Edge of Glory' are dance anthems about identity. The album debuted at number one in 20 countries. It is her most ambitious pop statement.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album mixes rock guitars, disco, and industrial beats. The title track became an anthem for the LGBTQ community.

name: Joanne
teaser: 2016 Lady Gaga's fifth album is her most personal: 'Million Reasons', 'Joanne', and 'Perfect Illusion' are stripped-back country-pop about family and loss. The album was named after her aunt who died at 19. It won a Grammy for Best Pop Vocal Album.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the shift — the album trades her dance sound for acoustic guitars and raw vocals. 'Million Reasons' became a fan favorite and live staple.

name: Chromatica
teaser: 2020 Lady Gaga's sixth album returned to pure dance pop: 'Stupid Love', 'Rain on Me', and '911' are euphoric and escapist. The album was recorded during a period of personal struggle. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — BloodPop and Burns crafted a cohesive electronic sound. 'Rain on Me' with Ariana Grande won a Grammy.

name: The Fame Monster
teaser: 2009 Lady Gaga's EP expanded her debut's universe: 'Bad Romance', 'Telephone', and 'Alejandro' are dark, theatrical, and iconic. The monster theme references her fears. The EP won three Grammys and sold 6 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the darkness — the songs are more experimental than the debut. 'Bad Romance' is one of the most awarded songs of the decade.

name: Section.80
teaser: 2011 Kendrick Lamar's debut album introduced his storytelling: 'HiiiPower', 'A.D.H.D', and 'Rigamortus' are socially conscious West Coast rap. The album was released independently and built his underground following. It set the stage for his major-label masterpieces.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the narrative — the album is a concept piece about a generation. 'A.D.H.D' became an anthem for his peers.

name: It Was Written
teaser: 1996 Nas's second album traded Illmatic's rawness for cinematic scope: 'If I Ruled the World', 'Street Dreams', and 'I Gave You Power' are grand and ambitious. The album sold 2.5 million copies. It is often debated as nearly the equal of his debut.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the storytelling — 'I Gave You Power' is told from the perspective of a gun. The production by Trackmasters gave the album a mafioso feel.

tracks.title: If I Ruled the World (Imagine That)

name: Stillmatic
teaser: 2001 Nas's fifth album reasserted his dominance: 'Ether', 'One Mic', and 'Got Ur Self a Gun' are combative and focused. The album was a response to rival Jay-Z's attacks. It re-established Nas as a top-tier rapper.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the diss — 'Ether' is one of the most brutal diss tracks in hip-hop history. The album's title signaled a return to his debut's spirit.

name: God's Son
teaser: 2002 Nas's sixth album blends street wisdom with spiritual reflection: 'Made You Look', 'I Can', and 'Dance' are incisive and personal. The album was released after his mother's death. It is among his most emotionally direct work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'I Can' — the song teaches children self-worth over a Beethoven sample. The album's title honors his mother.

name: The Score
teaser: 1996 The Fugees' second album fused hip-hop, soul, and reggae: 'Killing Me Softly', 'Fu-Gee-La', and 'Ready or Not' made them international stars. The album sold 18 million copies and won two Grammys. It remains the best-selling hip-hop album of its era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the covers — 'Killing Me Softly' turned a Roberta Flack classic into a global hit. The album's genre blend was unprecedented.

teaser: 1999 Dr. Dre's second album proved the G-funk architect still ruled: 'Still D.R.E.', 'The Next Episode', and 'Forgot About Dre' are West Coast anthems. The album relaunched Snoop and Eminem alongside Dre. It is the definitive West Coast album of its era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — every track is immaculately crafted. 'Still D.R.E.' features one of the most recognizable piano riffs in rap.

tracks.title: Fuck You (censored as F*** You in the edited version)
Bitch Niggaz (censored as Bi*** Ni**az in the edited version)

name: Compton
teaser: 2015 Dr. Dre's third album ended a 16-year gap: 'Talking to My Diary', 'One Shot One Kill', and 'Deep Water' are dense and cinematic. The album was released alongside the film Straight Outta Compton. It is his final statement as a rapper.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album features contributions from Kendrick Lamar and Anderson .Paak. It won a Grammy for Best Rap Album.

name: The Documentary
teaser: 2005 The Game's debut, executive-produced by Dr. Dre, made him a star: 'Hate It or Love It', 'How We Do', and 'Westside Story' are G-funk updates for the new century. The album sold 5 million copies. It is the last great West Coast debut.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Dre's beats anchor the album. 'Hate It or Love It' with 50 Cent became an anthem of rivalry.

name: Food & Liquor
teaser: 2006 Lupe Fiasco's debut is one of the most literate rap albums ever: 'Kick, Push', 'Daydreamin'', and 'Hurt Me Soul' are intricate and political. The album won a Grammy for Best Urban/Alternative Performance. It established him as hip-hop's poet.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the wordplay — Lupe's lyrics are dense with references and double meanings. 'Kick, Push' is a love song about skateboarding.

name: The Cool
teaser: 2007 Lupe Fiasco's second album expanded his debut's concept: 'Superstar', 'Paris, Tokyo', and 'The Cool' explore the characters he created. The album's production by Kanye West and others is cinematic. It is his most ambitious work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the narrative — the album follows the characters Michael Young History and The Cool. 'Superstar' became his biggest hit.

name: 808s & Heartbreak
teaser: 2008 Kanye West's fourth album traded rapping for autotuned singing: 'Love Lockdown', 'Heartless', and 'Street Lights' are sparse and melancholic. The album's grief after his mother's death and his broken engagement defined it. It influenced a decade of emo rap.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the 808 drums and minimal synth pads created a new template for rap. 'Love Lockdown' has no chorus in the traditional sense.

name: Yeezus
teaser: 2013 Kanye West's sixth album is his most abrasive: 'Black Skinhead', 'New Slaves', and 'Blood on the Leaves' are industrial, confrontational, and brilliant. The album was produced in six weeks with a team including Daft Punk. It is his most divisive work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the textures — the album is built from industrial noise, punk energy, and minimalist beats. 'Black Skinhead' has no traditional chorus.

name: The Life of Pablo
teaser: 2016 Kanye West's seventh album was revised and re-released repeatedly: 'Ultralight Beam', 'Famous', and 'Waves' are gospel, hip-hop, and chaos. The album's ever-changing nature was a statement about art in the streaming age. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the gospel — the album opens with church choir and Chance the Rapper. The tracklist changed even after release, a first for a major album.

name: Donda
teaser: 2021 Kanye West's tenth album was named for his late mother: 'Hurricane', 'Jail', and 'Moon' are gospel-tinged and grandiose. The album was unveiled at three listening events in stadiums. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the scale — the album is a two-hour gospel-rap epic. The listening events were as much performance art as music.

name: Watch the Throne
teaser: 2011 Jay-Z and Kanye West's collaboration album is a celebration of success: 'N****s in Paris', 'Otis', and 'No Church in the Wild' are maximalist and luxurious. The album sold over a million copies and won three Grammys. 'Paris' became a live spectacle.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album features samples of Otis Redding and James Brown. The live performances of 'Paris' were legendary for their repeated encores.

name: Kids See Ghosts
teaser: 2018 Kanye West and Kid Cudi's collaboration is a seven-track meditation on mental health: 'Reborn', '4th Dimension', and 'Kids See Ghosts' are raw and redemptive. The album was recorded in Wyoming in a week. It is one of the most acclaimed releases of its year.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the arc — the album moves from chaos to peace. 'Reborn' is an anthem about recovery and growth.

name: Meddle
teaser: 1971 Pink Floyd's sixth album foreshadowed their masterpiece: 'Echoes', 'One of These Days', and 'Fearless' are atmospheric and ambitious. The 23-minute 'Echoes' closes the album with their most complete statement to that point. It is the bridge to Dark Side of the Moon.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Echoes' — the song's underwater guitar and slow build define the band's sound. The album was recorded in bits across many studios.

name: Obscured by Clouds
teaser: 1972 Pink Floyd's soundtrack for the film La Vallee is an underrated gem: 'Wot's... Uh the Deal', 'Childhood's End', and 'Free Four' are melodic and relaxed. The album was recorded during a pause in the Dark Side sessions. It is their most underrated record.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the songs — the album is more straightforward than their epics. 'Childhood's End' is the only Pink Floyd song to mention a UFO.

name: Atom Heart Mother
teaser: 1970 Pink Floyd's fifth album features the 23-minute title suite with a choir and orchestra: 'Atom Heart Mother', 'If', and 'Summer '68' show the band moving toward their epic sound. The album reached number one in the UK. It is a transitional work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title suite — its orchestral and choral sections were controversial among fans. The album's cow cover is among the most famous in music.

tracks.title: Alan's Psychedelic Breakfast" :I. "Rise and Shine (3:33) :II. "Sunny Side Up (4:12) :III. "Morning Glory

name: A Saucerful of Secrets
teaser: 1968 Pink Floyd's second album was their first without Syd Barrett: 'Set the Controls for the Heart of the Sun', 'A Saucerful of Secrets', and 'Remember a Moment' show the band finding a new direction. The title track is a 12-minute instrumental epic. It is the beginning of their progressive era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — it builds from quiet murmurs to a full-band climax. The album was recorded as the band transformed.

tracks.title: Set the Controls for the Heart of the Sun
A Saucerful of Secrets :I. "Something Else (3:57) :II. "Syncopated Pandemonium (3:07) :III. "Storm Signal (1:34) :IV. "Celestial Voices

name: The Piper at the Gates of Dawn
teaser: 1967 Pink Floyd's debut is the sound of Syd Barrett's psychedelic genius: 'Astronomy Domine', 'Interstellar Overdrive', and 'Bike' are playful, strange, and revolutionary. The album was recorded at Abbey Road while the Beatles worked on Sgt. Pepper. It is the definitive psychedelic record.

exploreAction.targetName: The Piper at the Gates of Dawn (1967) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to Barrett's imagination — the songs mix nursery rhymes, space travel, and acid rock. The album's influence on psychedelia is immeasurable.

tracks.title: Take Up Thy Stethoscope and Walk

name: A Momentary Lapse of Reason
teaser: 1987 Pink Floyd's first album without Roger Waters: 'Learning to Fly', 'On the Turning Away', and 'Sorrow' are polished and optimistic. David Gilmour led the band into a new era. The album sold 7 million copies.

exploreAction.targetName: A Momentary Lapse of Reason (1987) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album was recorded largely on a houseboat studio. 'Learning to Fly' is about Gilmour's new pilot's license.

name: The Division Bell
teaser: 1994 Pink Floyd's final studio album: 'High Hopes', 'Marooned', and 'Take It Back' are atmospheric and elegiac. The album sold 12 million copies and won a Grammy for Best Rock Instrumental. It is a fitting farewell.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'High Hopes' — the song closes the album and the band's career with a sense of farewell. The album's title came from the gap between the band members.

tracks.title: What Do You Want from Me

name: Led Zeppelin
teaser: 1969 Led Zeppelin's debut redefined rock with its heaviness: 'Good Times Bad Times', 'Dazed and Confused', and 'Communication Breakdown' are blues-rock at maximum power. The album was recorded in 36 hours on a budget of 1,780 pounds. It sold 10 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the dynamics — the album's loud-quiet shifts were revolutionary. 'Dazed and Confused' was played live for over a decade.

name: Led Zeppelin II
teaser: 1969 Led Zeppelin's second album was recorded while touring: 'Whole Lotta Love', 'Heartbreaker', and 'Ramble On' are riff-driven and raw. The album's heavy blues sound defined hard rock. It sold 12 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the riffs — the album is built on Jimmy Page's heaviest guitar work. 'Whole Lotta Love' was built on a Willie Dixon blues song.

tracks.title: What Is and What Should Never Be
Living Loving Maid (She's Just a Woman)

name: Led Zeppelin III
teaser: 1970 Led Zeppelin's third album surprised fans with acoustic songs: 'Immigrant Song', 'Since I've Been Loving You', and 'Tangerine' balance electric and folk. The album was recorded at a Welsh cottage. It is their most varied early work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the range — from the metal of 'Immigrant Song' to the folk of 'Tangerine'. The album's cover features hidden images when rotated.

name: Houses of the Holy
teaser: 1973 Led Zeppelin's fifth album expanded beyond hard rock: 'The Song Remains the Same', 'No Quarter', and 'The Rain Song' are progressive and epic. The album was their first without a title. It sold 11 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the textures — the album incorporates reggae, funk, and orchestral elements. 'No Quarter' is one of their most atmospheric songs.

tracks.title: Over the Hills and Far Away

name: Presence
teaser: 1976 Led Zeppelin's seventh album was recorded during Robert Plant's recovery from a car crash: 'Achilles Last Stand', 'Nobody's Fault but Mine', and 'For Your Life' are relentless and guitar-driven. The album is their most intense work. It divided critics but has aged well.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Achilles Last Stand' — the song's galloping rhythm and layered guitars are a masterclass. The album was recorded in just three weeks.

name: In Through the Out Door
teaser: 1979 Led Zeppelin's final album: 'Fool in the Rain', 'All My Love', and 'I'm Gonna Crawl' show a band experimenting with keyboards and Latin rhythms. The album's packaging featured hidden images revealed by water. It sold 7 million copies despite mixed reviews.

exploreAction.targetName: In Through the Out Door (1979) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the experimentation — John Paul Jones's keyboards dominate the album. 'Fool in the Rain' features a samba section that showed their range.

name: Coda
teaser: 1982 Led Zeppelin's posthumous collection of outtakes: 'We're Gonna Groove', 'I Can't Quit You Baby', and 'Wearing and Tearing' are raw and unfinished. The album was released after John Bonham's death. It is a coda in the musical sense — a closing passage.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the raw takes — the album captures the band's live energy. 'Wearing and Tearing' was written in response to punk.

name: Fleetwood Mac
teaser: 1975 Fleetwood Mac's self-titled album with newcomers Lindsey Buckingham and Stevie Nicks transformed the band: 'Rhiannon', 'Landslide', and 'Say You Love Me' are California pop-rock at its best. The album sold 5 million copies and launched their golden era. It is the perfect introduction to the band.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the harmonies — Buckingham and Nicks added a new dimension to the band's sound. 'Rhiannon' was inspired by Welsh mythology.

name: Then Play On
teaser: 1969 Fleetwood Mac's third album is their last with Peter Green: 'Oh Well', 'Rattlesnake Shake', and 'Coming Your Way' are blues-rock at its most inventive. The album marks the end of the band's original era. It is a bridge between blues and rock.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Oh Well' — its flamenco-style guitar section was revolutionary for a blues band. The album's title reflects the band's improvisational approach.

name: Kiln House
teaser: 1970 Fleetwood Mac's fourth album without Peter Green: 'Station Man', 'Jewel Eyed Judy', and 'This Is the Rock' are rockabilly and blues. The band carried on with guitarist Jeremy Spencer and Danny Kirwan. The album is transitional but charming.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the rockabilly — the album is lighter than the band's blues work. The cover art features a famous pinup illustration.

tracks.title: Tell Me All the Things You Do

name: Rubber Soul
teaser: 1965 The Beatles' sixth album raised pop's ambitions: 'Norwegian Wood', 'In My Life', and 'Nowhere Man' are literate and introspective. The album's folk-rock sound and studio craft influenced everyone from the Beach Boys to Dylan. It is the album where the Beatles became artists.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the songwriting — 'In My Life' is one of the greatest songs ever written, with its harpsichord-style piano solo. The album was recorded in a month.

name: Help!
teaser: 1965 The Beatles' fifth album is a bridge from their pop era to their artistic peak: 'Help!', 'Ticket to Ride', and 'Yesterday' show growing sophistication. 'Yesterday' features a string quartet, a first for the band. The album accompanied their second film.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Yesterday' — Paul McCartney's ballad with a string quartet was a pop first. The album marks the start of the Beatles' most creative period.

tracks.title: You've Got to Hide Your Love Away
You're Going to Lose That Girl

name: Beatles for Sale
teaser: 1964 The Beatles' fourth album leans country and rockabilly: 'Eight Days a Week', 'I'll Follow the Sun', and 'No Reply' are melodic and assured. The album was recorded between tours. It shows the band's versatility beyond Beatlemania.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the country influence — the album includes covers of Carl Perkins and Buddy Holly. 'Eight Days a Week' was their first song with a fade-in.

tracks.title: I Don't Want to Spoil the Party
Everybody's Trying to Be My Baby

name: A Hard Day's Night
teaser: 1964 The Beatles' third album is the only one with all original songs: 'A Hard Day's Night', 'Can't Buy Me Love', and 'And I Love Her' are confident and catchy. The album accompanied their film of the same name. It is Beatlemania at its peak.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the opening chord — the album's first chord has been analyzed by musicians for decades. The film made the band global icons.

tracks.title: I'm Happy Just to Dance with You

name: With the Beatles
teaser: 1963 The Beatles' second album mixed originals with covers: 'All My Loving', 'It Won't Be Long', and 'Please Mr. Postman' show their R&B roots. The album's stark black-and-white cover was iconic. It spent 21 weeks at number one in the UK.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the covers — the band's versions of Motown and girl-group songs reveal their influences. 'All My Loving' became a live staple.

tracks.title: You Really Got a Hold on Me

name: Please Please Me
teaser: 1963 The Beatles' debut was recorded in a single day: 'I Saw Her Standing There', 'Love Me Do', and 'Twist and Shout' capture the band's raw live energy. The album launched Beatlemania. It spent 30 weeks at number one in the UK.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the energy — 'Twist and Shout' was recorded last, when John Lennon's voice was nearly gone. The album was recorded in 585 minutes.

tracks.title: Do You Want to Know a Secret

name: The Beatles
teaser: 1968 The Beatles' White Album is a double album of the band pulling apart: 'While My Guitar Gently Weeps', 'Blackbird', and 'Helter Skelter' show four solo careers in one record. The album's minimalist white cover was a reaction to Sgt. Pepper's excess. It is their most diverse work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the range — from the folk of 'Blackbird' to the metal of 'Helter Skelter'. Each member wrote alone, making it a collection of four voices.

tracks.title: The Continuing Story of Bungalow Bill
Why Don't We Do It in the Road?
Everybody's Got Something to Hide Except Me and My Monkey

teaser: 2000 The Beatles' compilation of all 27 of their UK number-one singles: 'Hey Jude', 'Yesterday', and 'Let It Be' trace their entire career. The album sold 31 million copies, making it the best-selling album of the 2000s. It is the definitive Beatles introduction.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the evolution — from 'Love Me Do' to 'The Long and Winding Road', the compilation shows the band's transformation. The album was remastered from the original tapes.

tracks.title: I Want to Hold Your Hand
The Ballad of John and Yoko

name: Smile
teaser: 2011 The Beach Boys' legendary unfinished album, finally released: 'Good Vibrations', 'Heroes and Villains', and 'Surf's Up' are Brian Wilson's most ambitious work. The album was abandoned in 1967 and reconstructed decades later. It is pop's greatest lost masterpiece.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the studio craft — the album's fragments were assembled from hours of sessions. 'Good Vibrations' alone took six months and cost $50,000.

tracks.title: I Love to Say Da Da
Old Master Painter" / "You Are My Sunshine
Child Is Father of the Man
I'm in Great Shape" / "I Wanna Be Around" / "Workshop

name: Sunflower
teaser: 1970 The Beach Boys' first album on their own label: 'Add Some Music to Your Day', 'This Whole World', and 'Forever' are warm and beautifully arranged. The album was a critical favorite that sold poorly. It is now regarded as one of their best.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the harmonies — the album features some of the band's most intricate vocal arrangements. 'Forever' was later covered by Dennis Wilson's friends.

tracks.title: Add Some Music to Your Day

name: Holland
teaser: 1973 The Beach Boys' ambitious album was recorded in the Netherlands: 'Sail On, Sailor', 'California Saga', and 'Funky Pretty' are sprawling and adventurous. The album was a modest hit and a critical favorite. It is the end of their classic era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Sail On, Sailor' — the song's build is one of the band's best. The album was recorded at a Dutch studio the band had to build themselves.

teaser: 1969 The Beach Boys' album assembled unreleased tracks: 'Do It Again', 'I Can Hear Music', and 'Bluebirds over the Mountain' are polished pop. The album was the last with Brian Wilson's full participation for years. It closed the 60s for the band.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the covers — the album includes a version of Phil Spector's 'I Can Hear Music'. The tracklist was assembled from scattered sessions.

name: Friends
teaser: 1968 The Beach Boys' gentle album of domestic bliss: 'Friends', 'Busy Doin' Nothin'', and 'Little Bird' are soft and experimental. The album was a commercial flop but a critical favorite. It is the band's most understated work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the calm — the album is a retreat from the psychedelic excess of the era. The recording sessions were some of the band's most relaxed.

tracks.title: When a Man Needs a Woman

name: Wild Honey
teaser: 1967 The Beach Boys' stripped-back album of R&B covers and originals: 'Wild Honey', 'Darlin'', and 'Mama Says' are funky and direct. The album was recorded at home in two months. It was a reaction to the complexity of Smile.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the simplicity — the album was recorded on a home tape machine. 'Darlin'' became a favorite live song.

tracks.title: I Was Made to Love Her
I'd Love Just Once to See You

name: Smiley Smile
teaser: 1967 The Beach Boys' album released in place of Smile: 'Good Vibrations', 'Heroes and Villains', and 'She's Goin' Bald' are strange and beautiful. The album baffled fans at release but has grown in reputation. It is the sound of an unfinished masterpiece.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the weirdness — the album's stripped-down versions of Smile songs sound like demos from another dimension. 'Good Vibrations' became their biggest hit.

tracks.title: Fall Breaks and Back to Winter (W. Woodpecker Symphony)

name: The Beach Boys Today!
teaser: 1965 The Beach Boys' album marked their artistic leap: 'California Girls', 'When I Grow Up', and 'Please Let Me Wonder' are sophisticated and personal. The album's second side was all ballads, a first for rock. It is their transition to genius.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the songwriting — Brian Wilson's production and lyrics matured dramatically. 'California Girls' is one of the most famous intros in pop.

tracks.title: When I Grow Up (To Be a Man)
In the Back of My Mind

name: All Summer Long
teaser: 1964 The Beach Boys' album of summer songs: 'I Get Around', 'All Summer Long', and 'Wendy' are sunny and sophisticated. The album spent five weeks at number one. It is the peak of their early surf era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the harmonies — the band's vocal blend was unmatched. 'I Get Around' was their first number-one single.

name: Surfer Girl
teaser: 1963 The Beach Boys' third album features their first self-produced single: 'Surfer Girl', 'Catch a Wave', and 'The Surfer Moon' are gentle and harmonic. The album shows Brian Wilson's growing studio ambition. It is a milestone of surf pop.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — its melody was inspired by a song Wilson heard in a dream. The album's production shows his early genius.

tracks.title: South Bay Surfer (The Old Folks at Home)

name: Surfin' U.S.A.
teaser: 1963 The Beach Boys' second album of surf anthems: 'Surfin' U.S.A.', 'Shut Down', and 'Surfer's Rule' are energetic and catchy. The album's title track borrowed Chuck Berry's melody. It made the band national stars.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the energy — the album captures the surf craze at its peak. 'Surfin' U.S.A.' was a top-five hit.

name: Surfin' Safari
teaser: 1962 The Beach Boys' debut captured the California surf scene: 'Surfin' Safari', '409', and 'Ten Little Indians' are energetic and naive. The album made the band local heroes. It is the beginning of the surf rock era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the innocence — the album is a time capsule of early 60s California. '409' celebrates the engine of a Chevy.

name: Brian Wilson
teaser: 2004 Brian Wilson's long-awaited solo album finally matched his legend: 'Love and Mercy', 'Gettin' in Over My Head', and 'Good Timin'' are warm and redemptive. The album was released after decades of struggle. It was his first fully realized solo work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album was produced with members of the Wondermints. 'Love and Mercy' became his anthem of hope.

tracks.title: Baby Let Your Hair Grow Long
Meet Me in My Dreams Tonight

name: Frank
teaser: 2003 Amy Winehouse's debut introduced her retro soul sound: 'Stronger Than Me', 'Take the Box', and 'Fuck Me Pumps' are jazzy and sharp. The album won a Brit Award and a Mercury Prize nomination. It showcased her voice and songwriting before her fame.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the jazz — the album's production is more understated than her later work. The lyrics are witty and confessional.

tracks.title: Amy Amy Amy / "Outro" / "Brother (hidden track) / "Mr Magic (Through the Smoke)
Amy Amy Amy / "Outro" / "Moody's Mood for Love (hidden track) / "Know You Now

name: Lioness: Hidden Treasures
teaser: 2011 Amy Winehouse's posthumous collection of unreleased songs: 'Our Day Will Come', 'Between the Cheats', and 'Half Time' show her range beyond the hits. The album was compiled by her friends and producers. It is a bittersweet final document.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the outtakes — the album includes early versions and unreleased gems. 'Our Day Will Come' was a 1963 pop song she made her own.

tracks.title: Will You Still Love Me Tomorrow?

name: In the Lonely Hour
teaser: 2014 Sam Smith's debut made heartbreak a global anthem: 'Stay with Me', 'I'm Not the Only One', and 'Lay Me Down' are soulful and sad. The album won four Grammys including Best Pop Vocal Album. It sold 12 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the emotion — Smith's voice carries the album's ache. 'Stay with Me' was written about a one-night stand.

name: Divide
teaser: 2017 Ed Sheeran's third album is a global smash: 'Shape of You', 'Castle on the Hill', and 'Perfect' blend pop, folk, and R&B. The album sold 26 million copies and was the best-selling album of 2017. 'Shape of You' became one of the most-streamed songs ever.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Benny Blanco and Steve Mac crafted radio-perfect hooks. The album's emotional songs became wedding staples.

name: Sweetener
teaser: 2018 Ariana Grande's fourth album processed grief into pop: 'God Is a Woman', 'Breathin'', and 'No Tears Left to Cry' are buoyant and vulnerable. The album won a Grammy for Best Pop Vocal Album. It marked her artistic maturation.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Pharrell Williams contributed several tracks with his signature sound. 'No Tears Left to Cry' was her first song after the Manchester bombing.

name: Thank U, Next
teaser: 2019 Ariana Grande's fifth album was recorded in two weeks: 'Thank U, Next', '7 Rings', and 'Break Up with Your Girlfriend' are confident and personal. The album debuted at number one and its title track broke streaming records. It is her most honest work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album was recorded quickly, giving it a raw energy. '7 Rings' samples the Sound of Music's 'My Favorite Things'.

tracks.title: Break Up with Your Girlfriend, I'm Bored

name: Positions
teaser: 2020 Ariana Grande's sixth album explores intimacy and lockdown life: 'Positions', '34+35', and 'POV' are smooth and playful. The album debuted at number one. It is her most mature and mellow work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album blends trap, R&B, and pop seamlessly. 'POV' closes the album with vulnerability.

name: Eternal Sunshine
teaser: 2024 Ariana Grande's seventh album is a confessional return: 'Yes, And?', 'We Can't Be Friends', and 'The Boy Is Mine' are danceable and direct. The album was inspired by the film of the same name. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the dance influences — the album blends 90s house with modern pop. 'We Can't Be Friends' was a global hit.

name: Yours Truly
teaser: 2013 Ariana Grande's debut introduced her as pop's new voice: 'The Way', 'Baby I', and 'Tattooed Heart' blend doo-wop and R&B. The album was recorded over three years with multiple producers. It set the stage for her superstardom.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the vocals — Grande's four-octave range is on full display. 'The Way' with Mac Miller was her breakthrough single.

name: My Everything
teaser: 2014 Ariana Grande's second album expanded her sound: 'Problem', 'Break Free', and 'Love Me Harder' are electro-pop anthems. The album debuted at number one and produced four top-ten singles. It made her a global star.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Max Martin and Zedd contributed to the album. 'Break Free' with Zedd became a dance anthem.

tracks.title: Just a Little Bit of Your Heart

name: Dangerous Woman
teaser: 2016 Ariana Grande's third album is her most confident: 'Dangerous Woman', 'Into You', and 'Side to Side' are sleek and seductive. The album debuted at number two and produced several hits. It is her artistic peak of the decade.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album blends pop, R&B, and dance with polish. 'Into You' is often cited as her best single.

name: reputation
teaser: 2017 Taylor Swift's sixth album is a dark reinvention: 'Look What You Made Me Do', 'Delicate', and '...Ready for It?' address her public battles with venom and wit. The album sold 4.5 million copies and debuted at number one. It is her most defiant work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Max Martin and Shellback crafted a darker electronic sound. 'Look What You Made Me Do' announced her new era.

tracks.title: Look What You Made Me Do
This Is Why We Can't Have Nice Things

teaser: 2014 Taylor Swift's fifth album was her full pivot to pop: 'Shake It Off', 'Blank Space', and 'Style' are shimmering synth-pop. The album sold 10 million copies and won Album of the Year at the Grammys. It is one of the best-selling albums of all time.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Max Martin and Shellback crafted the album's polished pop sound. 'Blank Space' satirized her media image.

tracks.title: All You Had to Do Was Stay

name: Speak Now
teaser: 2010 Taylor Swift's third album is entirely self-written: 'Mine', 'Back to December', and 'Enchanted' are confessional and mature. The album sold 5 million copies and debuted at number one. It is her most personal early work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the songwriting — Swift wrote every song alone, a rarity for a major pop album. 'Enchanted' became a fan favorite about a crush.

name: Fearless
teaser: 2008 Taylor Swift's second album made her a superstar: 'Love Story', 'You Belong with Me', and 'Fifteen' are country-pop perfection. The album won Album of the Year at the Grammys, making her the youngest winner ever. It sold 12 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the hooks — the album's choruses are built for stadiums. 'Love Story' was inspired by Romeo and Juliet with a happy ending.

tracks.title: Fearless Tour 2009 First Show Behind the Scenes

name: Taylor Swift
teaser: 2006 Taylor Swift's debut introduced country's new star: 'Tim McGraw', 'Teardrops on My Guitar', and 'Our Song' are teenage country-pop gems. The album sold 7 million copies. It is the beginning of her unprecedented career.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the innocence — the debut captures her teenage perspective. 'Our Song' was written for a school talent show.

name: Midnights
teaser: 2022 Taylor Swift's tenth album is a late-night meditation: 'Anti-Hero', 'Lavender Haze', and 'Karma' are moody and introspective. The album sold 5 million copies in its first year and won Album of the Year at the Grammys. It is her most personal album in years.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Jack Antonoff and Aaron Dessner crafted a cohesive synth-pop sound. 'Anti-Hero' is her most self-deprecating hit.

name: Evermore
teaser: 2020 Taylor Swift's ninth album is folklore's darker sister: 'Willow', 'Champagne Problems', and 'Coney Island' are folk songs about regret and winter. The album was recorded in the same quarantine sessions as folklore. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the storytelling — the album's songs are more narrative than folklore's. 'Champagne Problems' is a fan-favorite about a rejected proposal.

name: Lover
teaser: 2019 Taylor Swift's seventh album is a celebration: 'Lover', 'Cruel Summer', and 'ME!' are bright and colorful. The album debuted at number one and sold 3 million copies. It is her most joyful work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Jack Antonoff and Swift crafted a pop sound with indie touches. 'Cruel Summer' became a sleeper hit years after release.

tracks.title: It's Nice to Have a Friend

name: The Tortured Poets Department
teaser: 2024 Taylor Swift's eleventh album is a double record about heartbreak: 'Fortnight', 'Down Bad', and 'So Long, London' are literate and raw. The album's surprise second half doubled its runtime. It sold 2.6 million copies in its first week, a record.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Jack Antonoff and Aaron Dessner split the album's two halves. 'Fortnight' with Post Malone was the lead single.

tracks.title: My Boy Only Breaks His Favorite Toys
Who's Afraid of Little Old Me?
I Can Fix Him (No Really I Can)
I Can Do It with a Broken Heart
The Smallest Man Who Ever Lived

name: Mr. Morale & the Big Steppers
teaser: 2022 Kendrick Lamar's fifth album is a therapy session: 'N95', 'Die Hard', and 'Father Time' confront trauma, fame, and growth. The album debuted at number one and won a Grammy. It is his most personal and uncomfortable work.

exploreAction.targetName: Mr. Morale & the Big Steppers (2022) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the narrative — the album is structured as a therapy session with interludes. 'Auntie Diaries' addresses trans identity with empathy.

name: GNX
teaser: 2024 Kendrick Lamar's sixth album arrived unannounced: 'Squabble Up', 'TV Off', and 'Luther' are West Coast bangers with political edge. The album debuted at number one amid his feud with Drake. It is his most direct album in years.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album is built on West Coast G-funk samples. 'Squabble Up' became an instant hit.

name: Untitled Unmastered
teaser: 2016 Kendrick Lamar's collection of outtakes from To Pimp a Butterfly: 'Untitled 02', 'Untitled 05', and 'Untitled 08' are as strong as the album itself. The tracks were recorded during the TPAB sessions. It won a Grammy for Best Rap Album.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the jazz — the collection continues TPAB's free-jazz energy. 'Untitled 02' features jazz vocalist Bilal.

name: A Star Is Born
teaser: 2018 Lady Gaga and Bradley Cooper's soundtrack became a phenomenon: 'Shallow', 'Always Remember Us This Way', and 'I'll Never Love Again' are raw and powerful. The album won a Grammy for 'Shallow'. It sold 6 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Shallow' — the song's build from a whisper to a roar won the Oscar for Best Original Song. The album's country-rock production fits the film.

tracks.title: I Don't Know What Love Is
I'll Never Love Again (extended version) (performed by Gaga)

name: Love for Sale
teaser: 2021 Lady Gaga and Tony Bennett's final collaboration: 'Love for Sale', 'I Get a Kick Out of You', and 'Night and Day' are classic standards sung by legends. The album won a Grammy for Best Traditional Pop Vocal Album. It is Bennett's final album.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the duets — Bennett's voice and Gaga's blend beautifully on the standards. The album was recorded between Bennett's Alzheimer's diagnosis sessions.

tracks.title: I Get a Kick Out of You

name: Cheap Thrills
teaser: 1968 Big Brother and the Holding Company's second album captured Janis Joplin at her peak: 'Piece of My Heart', 'Summertime', and 'Ball and Chain' are raw, bluesy, and volcanic. The cover was drawn by underground cartoonist R. Crumb. The album reached number one and made Joplin a star.
byline: Big Brother and the Holding Company

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to Joplin's voice — it rasps, wails, and soars with unmatched power. The album was recorded live in the studio with the band playing together.

tracks.title: I Need a Man to Love

name: After the Gold Rush
teaser: 1970 Neil Young's third solo album is a masterpiece of longing: 'After the Gold Rush', 'Only Love Can Break Your Heart', and 'Southern Man' are folk-rock songs about love, apocalypse, and hope. The album was recorded in a basement with pianist Nils Lofgren. It defined his delicate, high voice.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the piano — Lofgren played many parts while Young focused on guitar and voice. 'Southern Man' sparked a response from Lynyrd Skynyrd.

tracks.title: Only Love Can Break Your Heart
Don't Let It Bring You Down
When You Dance I Can Really Love

name: Everybody Knows This Is Nowhere
teaser: 1969 Neil Young's second album introduced Crazy Horse: 'Cinnamon Girl', 'Cowgirl in the Sand', and 'Down by the River' are long, loud, and raw. The album was recorded in three days with the garage band. It is the sound of Young finding his electric voice.

exploreAction.targetName: Everybody Knows This Is Nowhere (1969) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitar interplay — Young and Danny Whitten trade solos throughout. 'Down by the River' is nine minutes of slow-burning tension.

name: On the Beach
teaser: 1974 Neil Young's bleak masterpiece: 'Walk On', 'On the Beach', and 'Revolution Blues' are sardonic and weary. The album was a deliberate downer after his commercial peak. It has become a cult favorite among his fans.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the despair — the album was Young's response to the failures of the counterculture. 'Revolution Blues' is about the Manson murders.

tracks.title: See the Sky About to Rain

name: Zuma
teaser: 1975 Neil Young and Crazy Horse reunited for a loose, powerful album: 'Cortez the Killer', 'Lookin' for a Love', and 'Barstool Blues' are long, loud, and lyrical. The album was recorded quickly after years of strain. 'Cortez the Killer' is among his greatest songs.
