exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitars — Young's solos on 'Cortez the Killer' are among his most emotional. The album was recorded live in the studio with few overdubs.

name: Comes a Time
teaser: 1978 Neil Young's gentle country album: 'Comes a Time', 'Goin' Back', and 'Motorcycle Mama' are warm and acoustic. The album was recorded with a country band and a string section. It is his most accessible work of the 70s.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the harmonies — Nicolette Larson sings throughout the album. The title track is a meditation on change.

name: Rust Never Sleeps
teaser: 1979 Neil Young's live album with studio overdubs: 'My My, Hey Hey (Out of the Blue)', 'Powderfinger', and 'Welfare Mothers' capture his acoustic and electric sides. The album was recorded live with Crazy Horse. It is the sound of punk and classic rock meeting.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the acoustic-electric split — the album opens quiet and closes loud. 'Powderfinger' is a story song about a family tragedy.

tracks.title: My My, Hey Hey (Out of the Blue)
Hey Hey, My My (Into the Black)

name: Freedom
teaser: 1989 Neil Young's comeback album: 'Rockin' in the Free World', 'Crime in the City', and 'No More' are loud and political. The album marked his return to the electric sound after a decade of detours. It re-established him as a rock icon.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the anger — 'Rockin' in the Free World' is a protest anthem with a screaming guitar solo. The album was a bridge to the 90s grunge era.

tracks.title: Crime in the City (Sixty to Zero Part I)

name: Fleet Foxes
teaser: 2008 Fleet Foxes' debut made indie folk a movement: 'White Winter Hymnal', 'Ragged Wood', and 'Blue Ridge Mountains' are lush, harmonic, and timeless. The band's layered vocal harmonies evoked the Beach Boys and Appalachian choirs. The album was a critical and commercial breakthrough.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the harmonies — the band stacks voices in intricate arrangements. 'White Winter Hymnal' was built around a simple, nursery-rhyme melody.

name: Helplessness Blues
teaser: 2011 Fleet Foxes' second album deepened their sound: 'Helplessness Blues', 'Bedouin Dress', and 'The Shrine/An Argument' are ambitious and introspective. The album explores identity and uncertainty. It is their most complete statement.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the arrangements — the band moved beyond folk into chamber pop and psychedelia. The title track is a meditation on purpose.

name: Crack-Up
teaser: 2017 Fleet Foxes' third album was their most experimental: 'Third of May/Odaigahara', 'If You Need to, Keep Time on Me', and 'On Another Ocean (January/June)' are long and intricate. The album was inspired by F. Scott Fitzgerald's essay of the same name. It is their most ambitious work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the song structures — many tracks shift between movements. The album rewards patient, focused listening.

tracks.title: I Am All That I Need / Arroyo Seco / Thumbprint Scar
If You Need to, Keep Time on Me

name: Shore
teaser: 2020 Fleet Foxes' fourth album arrived on the autumn equinox: 'Can I Believe You', 'Sunblind', and 'Featherweight' are warm and hopeful. The album was recorded with collaborators across the globe during lockdown. It is their most optimistic work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the collaborations — the album features contributions from many indie artists. 'Sunblind' is a tribute to musicians the band lost.

tracks.title: A Long Way Past the Past

name: Hail to the Thief
teaser: 2003 Radiohead's sixth album balanced their experimental side with rock songs: 'There There', '2 + 2 = 5', and 'Sail to the Moon' are urgent and uneasy. The album was recorded in a church in two weeks. It is their last album with a traditional band sound for years.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the tension — the album was written in the shadow of the Iraq war. 'There There' became their biggest single in years.

tracks.title: Where I End and You Begin.

name: A Moon Shaped Pool
teaser: 2016 Radiohead's ninth album is their most elegiac: 'Burn the Witch', 'Daydreaming', and 'True Love Waits' are slow, string-laden, and beautiful. The album was five years in the making. 'True Love Waits' had been played live for two decades before finally being recorded.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the strings — the London Contemporary Orchestra plays throughout. The album closes with a piano ballad about loss.

tracks.title: Tinker Tailor Soldier Sailor Rich Man Poor Man Beggar Man Thief

name: Pablo Honey
teaser: 1993 Radiohead's debut introduced 'Creep', their accidental global hit: 'Creep', 'Anyone Can Play Guitar', and 'Stop Whispering' are grunge-era rock. The band was unhappy with the album's generic sound. It set the stage for their later genius.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Creep' — its sudden loud chorus was the band's breakthrough. The album is best heard as a rough sketch of what came next.

name: The King of Limbs
teaser: 2011 Radiohead's eighth album is a study in rhythm: 'Lotus Flower', 'Bloom', and 'Codex' are built on looping, fractured beats. The album was recorded with the band's live looping techniques. It is their most rhythm-focused work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the drums — the album is built around drum loops and percussion. 'Lotus Flower' became famous for Thom Yorke's dance in the video.

name: Harlequin
teaser: 2024 Lady Gaga's companion album to Joker: Folie a Deux: 'Folie a Deux', 'Happy Mistake', and 'The Joker' are torch songs and jazz standards. The album showcases her voice without pop production. It is a stylistic departure.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the vocals — the album strips away production to showcase her range. 'Folie a Deux' is an original song for the film.

tracks.title: If My Friends Could See Me Now

name: Mayhem
teaser: 2025 Lady Gaga's seventh studio album is a return to maximalist pop: 'Disease', 'Abracadabra', and 'Garden of Eden' blend her early electro sound with new textures. The album was announced as a homecoming to her roots. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album blends her signature electro-pop with live instruments. 'Abracadabra' became an instant fan favorite.

tracks.title: How Bad Do U Want Me

name: Cheek to Cheek
teaser: 2014 Lady Gaga and Tony Bennett's first duet album: 'Anything Goes', 'Cheek to Cheek', and 'I Can't Give You Anything but Love' are jazz standards sung with relish. The album won a Grammy for Best Traditional Pop Vocal Album. It introduced Gaga's voice to a new audience.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the chemistry — Bennett's mentoring shines through the duets. The album was recorded live with a jazz band.

tracks.title: I Can't Give You Anything but Love
Let's Face the Music and Dance
It Don't Mean a Thing (If It Ain't Got That Swing)
Bang Bang (My Baby Shot Me Down)
On a Clear Day (You Can See Forever)

name: White Light/White Heat
teaser: 1968 The Velvet Underground's second album is their loudest: 'White Light/White Heat', 'Sister Ray', and 'I Heard Her Call My Name' are harsh, noisy, and confrontational. The album was recorded in a day. It is noise rock's founding document.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the chaos — 'Sister Ray' is a 17-minute jam about sailors and drugs. The album's guitar feedback was a decade ahead of punk.

tracks.title: I Heard Her Call My Name

name: The Modern Lovers
teaser: 1976 The Modern Lovers' sole album was recorded in 1972 but released four years later: 'Roadrunner', 'Pablo Picasso', and 'She Cracked' are proto-punk songs about Boston and girls. The album's naive sound influenced punk and new wave. It is a cult classic.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the simplicity — the album is built on two chords and Jonathan Richman's deadpan vocals. 'Roadrunner' became an anthem of teenage freedom.

name: Adventure
teaser: 1978 Television's second album is softer and more polished than their debut: 'Foxhole', 'Glory', and 'Ain't That Nothin'' are melodic and intricate. The album was a commercial disappointment but has aged well. It is the band's farewell for decades.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the melodies — the album is more song-oriented than Marquee Moon. 'Glory' is a wry comment on the band's fame.

name: Moondance
teaser: 1970 Van Morrison's second album is his most accessible: 'Moondance', 'Crazy Love', and 'Into the Mystic' are warm, jazzy, and romantic. The album blended R&B, jazz, and folk into a new sound. It sold 4 million copies and is his best-selling work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the horn arrangements — the album's jazz-tinged R&B is infectious. 'Into the Mystic' is among the most loved songs in pop.

name: Tupelo Honey
teaser: 1971 Van Morrison's fifth album is warm and rootsy: 'Tupelo Honey', 'Wild Night', and 'These Dreams of You' are soulful and celebratory. The album was recorded with a band in a cabin. It is his most relaxed work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the band — the album was recorded live in a studio built in a cabin. 'Wild Night' became a cover favorite.

tracks.title: (Straight to Your Heart) Like a Cannonball
When That Evening Sun Goes Down

name: Saint Dominic's Preview
teaser: 1972 Van Morrison's sixth album spans soul, jazz, and Celtic folk: 'Jackie Wilson Said', 'Saint Dominic's Preview', and 'Almost Independence Day' are ambitious and varied. The album was recorded in multiple cities. It is his most eclectic work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the range — the album moves from funk to folk to rock. 'Almost Independence Day' is a 10-minute epic about the Northern Ireland troubles.

tracks.title: Jackie Wilson Said (I'm in Heaven When You Smile)

name: Veedon Fleece
teaser: 1974 Van Morrison's ninth album is his most introspective: 'Veedon Fleece', 'You Don't Pull No Punches, But You Don't Push the River', and 'Streets of Arklow' are long, poetic, and mystical. The album was inspired by a trip to Ireland. It is a cult favorite.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the poetry — the album's lyrics are among Morrison's most abstract. 'Veedon Fleece' is a meditation on wandering.

tracks.title: You Don't Pull No Punches, but You Don't Push the River

name: Wavelength
teaser: 1978 Van Morrison's album marked his turn to a rock band sound: 'Wavelength', 'Kingdom Hall', and 'Checkin' It Out' are polished and direct. The album was his first with a horn section in years. It reached number 28 on the Billboard chart.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album was recorded in Los Angeles with a full band. 'Wavelength' was inspired by a song he heard on the radio.

tracks.title: Take It Where You Find It

name: Into the Music
teaser: 1979 Van Morrison's album of spiritual longing: 'Bright Side of the Road', 'Into the Music', and 'Full Force Gale' are joyful and mystical. The album marked a return to his Celtic roots. It is a fan favorite.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the gospel influence — the album's backing singers lift every song. 'Bright Side of the Road' became a live staple.

tracks.title: You Make Me Feel So Free
It's All in the Game (Charles Dawes, Carl Sigman)
You Know What They're Writing About

name: Common One
teaser: 1980 Van Morrison's most mystical album: 'When Heart Is Open', 'Summertime in England', and 'Satisfied Mind' are long, meditative, and transcendental. The album was recorded in a French monastery. It divided critics but has a devoted following.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the length — the songs run 10-15 minutes each, built on meditative grooves. The album rewards patience and solitude.

name: Beautiful Vision
teaser: 1982 Van Morrison's album of spiritual devotion: 'Vanlose Stairway', 'Cleaning Windows', and 'Dweller on the Threshold' are tender and luminous. The album reflects his growing mysticism. It is among his most beautiful records.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the piano — the album features Mark Isham's trumpet and a contemplative mood. 'Cleaning Windows' is a nostalgic portrait of youth.

tracks.title: Across the Bridge Where Angels Dwell

name: Avalon Sunset
teaser: 1989 Van Morrison's album of duets and devotion: 'Whenever God Shines His Light', 'Have I Told You Lately', and 'I'd Love to Write Another Song' are warm and spiritual. The album was his biggest hit in years. 'Have I Told You Lately' became a wedding standard.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the duets — Cliff Richard joins him on 'Whenever God Shines His Light'. The album's spiritual themes are front and center.

tracks.title: Whenever God Shines His Light (duet with Cliff Richard)
I'd Love to Write Another Song
When Will I Ever Learn to Live in God

name: Enlightenment
teaser: 1990 Van Morrison's album of midlife reflection: 'Enlightenment', 'Real Real Gone', and 'In the Days Before Rock 'n' Roll' are witty and warm. The album's title track asks what enlightenment is. It is among his most personal works.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the wordplay — Morrison's lyrics are at their most playful. The album balances jazz, R&B, and Celtic sounds.

tracks.title: In the Days Before Rock 'N' Roll (Durcan, Morrison)

name: Hymns to the Silence
teaser: 1991 Van Morrison's double album is his most sprawling: 'When Will I Learn to Learn to Stop and Start?', 'I Need Your Kind of Loving', and 'See Me Through' span blues, gospel, and jazz. The album is a compendium of his influences.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the range — the double album covers every style he has touched. 'When Will I Learn' is a standout meditation.

tracks.title: I Can't Stop Loving You – (Gibson) – 3:54 (With The Chieftains)
See Me Through, Pt. 2 (Just a Closer Walk with Thee) – (Traditional)
Be Thou My Vision – (Traditional) – 3:49 (With The Chieftains)
I Need Your Kind of Loving

name: Days Like This
teaser: 1995 Van Morrison's return to form: 'Days Like This', 'Perfect Fit', and 'No Religion' are warm, confident, and melodic. The album was his most accessible in years. The title track became an anthem of contentment.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the groove — the album's band plays with ease. 'Days Like This' became his signature late-career song.

tracks.title: You Don't Know Me (Eddy Arnold, Cindy Walker)
I'll Never Be Free (Bennie Benjamin, George David Weiss)

name: The Healing Game
teaser: 1997 Van Morrison's album of deep grooves: 'The Healing Game', 'Rough God Goes Riding', and 'Fire in the Belly' are bluesy, earthy, and hypnotic. The album was recorded live in the studio. It is among his best late-period records.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the band — the album was cut live with a tight group. 'The Healing Game' is built on a slow, patient groove.

tracks.title: Piper at the Gates of Dawn

name: Back on Top
teaser: 1999 Van Morrison's bluesy return: 'Back on Top', 'Goin' Down Geneva', and 'Precious Time' are loose, funny, and direct. The album was his most immediate in years. It is a fan favorite.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the horns — the album's backing band includes a full horn section. 'Back on Top' has a swagger missing from his spiritual albums.

tracks.title: When the Leaves Come Falling Down
Valley of Tears – 5:02 (Fats Domino, arranged Morrison)

name: Keep It Simple
teaser: 2008 Van Morrison's album of stripped-back songs: 'Keep It Simple', 'Behind the Ritual', and 'End of the Land' are gentle and reflective. The album was recorded quickly with a small band. It is his most direct work of the 2000s.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the simplicity — the album avoids the mystical length of his other work. The title track is a statement of intent.

name: Erotica
teaser: 1992 Madonna's fifth album is her most explicit: 'Erotica', 'Deeper and Deeper', and 'Rain' are dance music about desire and intimacy. The album was tied to her book Sex, causing controversy. It is now considered one of her most daring records.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Shep Pettibone's house beats give the album its pulse. 'Deeper and Deeper' became a dance classic.

name: Bedtime Stories
teaser: 1994 Madonna's sixth album softened her image: 'Secret', 'Take a Bow', and 'Bedtime Story' are smooth R&B ballads. The album was a response to the backlash against Erotica. It is her most tender work of the decade.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album blends R&B with ambient textures. 'Take a Bow' with Babyface was her longest-running number one.

name: Prairie Wind
teaser: 2005 Neil Young's album of reflection, recorded before his brain surgery: 'The Painter', 'When God Made Me', and 'Prairie Wind' are gentle, nostalgic, and grateful. The album was recorded in Nashville. It is his most personal work of the decade.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album was recorded with a full band including Emmylou Harris. The title track looks back at his prairie childhood.

tracks.title: Falling Off the Face of the Earth

name: Sleeps with Angels
teaser: 1994 Neil Young and Crazy Horse's dark album about the death of Kurt Cobain: 'Sleeps with Angels', 'Change Your Mind', and 'Blue Eden' are long, slow, and haunted. The album was recorded in the studio where Cobain died. It is their heaviest work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the mood — the album is a meditation on mortality. The title track was directly inspired by Cobain's suicide note.

name: Little Broken Hearts
teaser: 2012 Norah Jones' fifth album, produced by Danger Mouse, is her most adventurous: 'Happy Pills', 'Little Broken Hearts', and 'Miriam' are moody, cinematic, and slightly sinister. The album was written during a breakup. It is a departure from her jazz-pop comfort zone.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Danger Mouse built the album's sparse, dark sound. 'Happy Pills' has a sinister edge beneath its catchy melody.

name: American Pie
teaser: 1971 Don McLean's album featuring the epic 'American Pie' — an eight-minute allegory about the death of rock and roll. 'Vincent', 'Crossroads', and 'Castles in the Air' are folk songs of loss and reflection. The title track is one of the most analyzed songs in pop.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the storytelling — 'American Pie' is a coded history of the 1960s. 'Vincent' is a tribute to Van Gogh written after reading his letters.

name: Squeeze
teaser: 1973 The Velvet Underground's final album without Lou Reed: 'Little Jack', 'She'll Make You Cry', and 'Sweet Bonnie Brown' are demo-quality rock. The album was rejected by the label and shelved for a decade. It is a curiosity for completists.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the raw demos — the album was recorded after the band's core had left. It is best understood as a coda to their story.

name: Live Rust
teaser: 1979 Neil Young's live double album with Crazy Horse: 'Hey Hey, My My', 'Powderfinger', and 'Like a Hurricane' capture the band's power on stage. The album was recorded during the Rust Never Sleeps tour. It is the definitive live Neil Young document.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the energy — Crazy Horse at their loudest and loosest. The album closes with a version of 'Tonight's the Night'.

tracks.title: My My, Hey Hey (Out of the Blue)
When You Dance I Can Really Love
The Needle and the Damage Done
Hey Hey, My My (Into the Black)

name: The Freewheelin' Bob Dylan
teaser: 1963 Bob Dylan's second album made him the voice of a generation: 'Blowin' in the Wind', 'A Hard Rain's A-Gonna Fall', and 'Don't Think Twice, It's All Right' are protest songs and love songs. The album sold 10 million copies. It is the beginning of his legend.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the writing — the album marked his leap from folk covers to original genius. 'Blowin' in the Wind' became an anthem of the civil rights movement.

tracks.title: Don't Think Twice, It's All Right
Honey, Just Allow Me One More Chance
Let Me Die in My Footsteps

name: The Times They Are A-Changin'
teaser: 1964 Bob Dylan's third album is his most political: 'The Times They Are A-Changin'', 'The Lonesome Death of Hattie Carroll', and 'Only a Pawn in Their Game' are protest songs of rare power. The album captures the civil rights era. It is his most committed work.

exploreAction.targetName: The Times They Are A-Changin' (1964) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the anger — the album is entirely acoustic and entirely political. 'The Lonesome Death of Hattie Carroll' tells a true story of injustice.

tracks.title: Only a Pawn in Their Game
The Lonesome Death of Hattie Carroll

name: Bringing It All Back Home
teaser: 1965 Bob Dylan's fifth album mixed acoustic songs with his first electric recordings: 'Mr. Tambourine Man', 'Subterranean Homesick Blues', and 'It's Alright, Ma' are a bridge between folk and rock. The album's electric side changed music history. It is the hinge of his career.

exploreAction.targetName: Bringing It All Back Home (1965) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the transition — side one is electric, side two is acoustic. 'Subterranean Homesick Blues' introduced his rapid-fire lyrical style.

tracks.title: It's All Over Now, Baby Blue

name: John Wesley Harding
teaser: 1967 Bob Dylan's quiet album after his motorcycle crash: 'All Along the Watchtower', 'I Dreamed I Saw St. Augustine', and 'The Ballad of Frankie Lee and Judas Priest' are spare, biblical, and mysterious. The album was a radical retreat from the psychedelic era. It is among his most enduring works.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the restraint — the album is acoustic trio recordings with no production. 'All Along the Watchtower' was made famous by Jimi Hendrix's cover.

tracks.title: As I Went Out One Morning
I Dreamed I Saw St. Augustine
The Ballad of Frankie Lee and Judas Priest

name: Nashville Skyline
teaser: 1969 Bob Dylan's country album with Johnny Cash: 'Lay Lady Lay', 'Girl from the North Country', and 'Tonight I'll Be Staying Here with You' are warm, melodic, and unexpected. Dylan sang in a new, softer voice. The album was a commercial success.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the voice — Dylan's new country croon surprised everyone. The duet with Johnny Cash on 'Girl from the North Country' is a historic meeting.

tracks.title: Tell Me That It Isn't True
Tonight I'll Be Staying Here with You

name: New Morning
teaser: 1970 Bob Dylan's gentle album after years of retreat: 'If Not for You', 'New Morning', and 'Sign on the Window' are warm and domestic. The album was a return to simplicity. It is among his most relaxed records.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the calm — the album was recorded with a small band including George Harrison on guitar. 'If Not for You' was covered by George Harrison.

name: Planet Waves
teaser: 1974 Bob Dylan's album with the Band: 'Forever Young', 'Something There Is About You', and 'Going, Going, Gone' are warm and rootsy. The album was recorded in three days. 'Forever Young' became a standard.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the Band — their backing gives the album a lived-in sound. 'Forever Young' is one of Dylan's most beloved songs.

name: The Basement Tapes
teaser: 1975 Bob Dylan and the Band's legendary basement recordings: 'I Shall Be Released', 'You Ain't Goin' Nowhere', and 'The Mighty Quinn' were recorded in 1967 at the Band's house. The songs were circulated as bootlegs for years before official release. They defined the Americana genre.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the intimacy — the recordings capture friends playing in a basement. 'The Mighty Quinn' became a hit for Manfred Mann.

tracks.title: Yea! Heavy and a Bottle of Bread
Crash on the Levee (Down in the Flood)

name: Desire
teaser: 1976 Bob Dylan's album of long, cinematic story songs: 'Hurricane', 'One More Cup of Coffee', and 'Sara' are sweeping and theatrical. The album was recorded in five days with violinist Scarlet Rivera. 'Hurricane' tells the story of boxer Rubin Carter.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the violin — Rivera's playing weaves through every song. 'Hurricane' is a 9-minute protest song about a wrongful conviction.

name: Street-Legal
teaser: 1978 Bob Dylan's album of hot-rodded gospel rock: 'Changing of the Guards', 'Baby, Stop Crying', and 'Is Your Love in Vain?' are dense, theatrical, and intense. The album's production was controversial. It has been reassessed as a strong late-70s work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the horns and female backing vocals — the album's sound is unlike anything else in his catalog. 'Changing of the Guards' is an epic opener.

tracks.title: Where Are You Tonight? (Journey Through Dark Heat)

name: Slow Train Coming
teaser: 1979 Bob Dylan's first gospel album: 'Gotta Serve Somebody', 'Slow Train', and 'Precious Angel' are born-again Christian songs with a funky band. The album won a Grammy for Best Male Rock Vocal. It divided fans but is musically strong.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the band — Mark Knopfler of Dire Straits plays guitar. 'Gotta Serve Somebody' was covered by many artists.

tracks.title: Gonna Change My Way of Thinking
Do Right to Me Baby (Do Unto Others)
Man Gave Names to All the Animals

name: Oh Mercy
teaser: 1989 Bob Dylan's return to critical favor: 'Everything Is Broken', 'Most of the Time', and 'Man in the Long Black Coat' are produced by Daniel Lanois. The album's swampy, mysterious sound was his best in a decade. It re-established him.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Lanois gave the album its atmospheric, haunted sound. 'Man in the Long Black Coat' is a voodoo-tinged mystery.

tracks.title: Man in the Long Black Coat

name: Time Out of Mind
teaser: 1997 Bob Dylan's late-career masterpiece: 'Love Sick', 'Not Dark Yet', and 'Make You Feel My Love' are brooding, world-weary, and profound. The album won Album of the Year at the Grammys, his first since 1970. It began his late renaissance.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the mood — the album was recorded with producer Daniel Lanois in sessions that became legendary. 'Not Dark Yet' is a meditation on mortality.

tracks.title: Til I Fell in Love with You

name: Love and Theft
teaser: 2001 Bob Dylan's thirtieth album: 'Mississippi', 'Summer Days', and 'Tweedle Dee & Tweedle Dum' are funny, bluesy, and loose. The album was recorded in two weeks with his touring band. It is his most playful work of the modern era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the band — the album was cut live in the studio. 'Mississippi' was rejected from Time Out of Mind and became a highlight here.

name: Modern Times
teaser: 2006 Bob Dylan's third album of his late renaissance: 'Thunder on the Mountain', 'When the Deal Goes Down', and 'Ain't Talkin'' are blues, folk, and country songs about love and the end of the world. The album debuted at number one, his first in 30 years.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the age — Dylan's voice is a gravelly instrument that carries the songs. The album's apocalyptic undertones are unmistakable.

name: Together Through Life
teaser: 2009 Bob Dylan's album of Tex-Mex blues: 'Beyond Here Lies Nothin'', 'Life Is Hard', and 'I Feel a Change Comin' On' are warm, funny, and seasoned. The album was written quickly with Grateful Dead lyricist Robert Hunter. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the accordion — the album has a Mexican border feel. The lyrics were co-written with Robert Hunter of the Grateful Dead.

tracks.title: If You Ever Go to Houston
I Feel a Change Comin' On

name: Tempest
teaser: 2012 Bob Dylan's 35th album: 'Duquesne Whistle', 'Pay in Blood', and 'Tempest' are long, dark, and masterful. The album's 14-minute title track recounts the Titanic sinking. It is among his most forceful late works.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the storytelling — the album is filled with narratives of murder, love, and disaster. 'Tempest' is a grim epic.

name: Rough and Rowdy Ways
teaser: 2020 Bob Dylan's first album of new songs in eight years: 'Murder Most Foul', 'I Contain Multitudes', and 'Key West (Philosopher Pirate)' are long, literary, and profound. The 17-minute 'Murder Most Foul' about the JFK assassination was a surprise hit. It is his late masterpiece.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the poetry — the album's lyrics are among his most dense and allusive. 'Murder Most Foul' references dozens of songs and events.

tracks.title: I've Made Up My Mind to Give Myself to You

name: Check Your Head
teaser: 1992 The Beastie Boys' fourth album returned to their roots: 'So What'cha Want', 'Pass the Mic', and 'Gratitude' blend rap with live funk. The band played their own instruments for the first time. It is their most organic work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the live band — the album was recorded with the group playing real instruments. 'Pass the Mic' is a dense, playful manifesto.

name: Ill Communication
teaser: 1994 The Beastie Boys' fifth album mixed rap, punk, and funk: 'Sabotage', 'Sure Shot', and 'Root Down' are furious and fun. The album debuted at number one. 'Sabotage' became famous for its music video.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the range — the album jumps from hardcore punk to smooth jazz. 'Sabotage' is a hardcore blast with a legendary video.

tracks.title: B-Boys Makin' with the Freak Freak

name: Hello Nasty
teaser: 1998 The Beastie Boys' sixth album was their most futuristic: 'Intergalactic', 'Body Movin'', and 'Remote Control' blend sci-fi samples with their signature raps. The album won a Grammy for Best Alternative Music Album. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the samples — the album is packed with odd, funky breaks. 'Intergalactic' became a global hit with its robot-voice chorus.

name: To the 5 Boroughs
teaser: 2004 The Beastie Boys' album about New York after 9/11: 'Ch-Check It Out', 'An Open Letter to NYC', and 'Triple Trouble' are political and defiant. The album was their first without Adam Yauch's usual voice. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the message — the album directly addresses the attacks and the city's recovery. 'An Open Letter to NYC' is a love letter to their home.

name: Hot Sauce Committee Part Two
teaser: 2011 The Beastie Boys' final album: 'Make Some Noise', 'Too Many Rappers', and 'Don't Play No Game That I Can't Win' are playful, funky, and defiant. The album was released while Adam Yauch battled cancer. It is a fitting farewell.

exploreAction.targetName: Hot Sauce Committee Part Two (2011) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the energy — the album sounds like three friends having fun. 'Make Some Noise' has a star-studded video.

tracks.title: Don't Play No Game That I Can't Win
Here's a Little Something for Ya

name: License to Ill
teaser: 1986 The Beastie Boys' debut made rap a party: 'Fight for Your Right', 'No Sleep till Brooklyn', and 'Brass Monkey' are bratty, loud, and catchy. The album was the first rap LP to top the Billboard chart. It sold 10 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Rick Rubin's beats are minimal and huge. 'Fight for Your Right' became an anthem of teenage rebellion.

name: The Blue Album
teaser: 1994 Weezer's debut made nerd-rock mainstream: 'Buddy Holly', 'Undone (The Sweater Song)', and 'Say It Ain't So' are power-pop perfection. The album's video for 'Buddy Holly' spliced the band into Happy Days. It sold 3 million copies and launched Rivers Cuomo's career.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Ric Ocasek of the Cars produced the album's clean, punchy sound. 'Say It Ain't So' is a dark song about family.

tracks.title: The World Has Turned and Left Me Here

name: Pinkerton
teaser: 1996 Weezer's second album was a commercial flop that became a cult classic: 'El Scorcho', 'Pink Triangle', and 'Across the Sea' are raw, confessional, and awkward. The album's honesty alienated fans at the time. It is now considered a masterpiece.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the rawness — the album was recorded quickly with a heavier sound. 'El Scorcho' is about a crush on someone with different taste.

name: Maladroit
teaser: 2002 Weezer's fourth album is their heaviest: 'Dope Nose', 'Keep Fishin'', and 'Slob' are punchy and immediate. The album was recorded in a month with input from fans. It reached number three on the Billboard chart.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitars — the album's metal riffs are a departure from their pop sound. 'Keep Fishin'' has a Muppets music video.

name: Make Believe
teaser: 2005 Weezer's fifth album is their most polished: 'Beverly Hills', 'Perfect Situation', and 'This Is Such a Pity' are radio-ready pop-rock. The album was their first platinum release since Pinkerton. 'Beverly Hills' became their biggest hit.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Rick Rubin produced the album's clean sound. 'Beverly Hills' was a response to their celebrity status.

name: The Red Album
teaser: 2008 Weezer's sixth album features all four members singing lead: 'Pork and Beans', 'Troublemaker', and 'The Greatest Man That Ever Lived' are eclectic and ambitious. The album was a return to their experimental streak. 'Pork and Beans' has a famous internet video.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the variety — the album spans power pop, metal, and ballads. 'Pork and Beans' references dozens of viral videos.

name: Raditude
teaser: 2009 Weezer's seventh album is their most pop-oriented: '(If You're Wondering If I Want You to) I Want You to', 'Can't Stop Partying', and 'Memories' are glossy and catchy. The album was co-written with outside hitmakers. It divided fans.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the pop — the album was a deliberate attempt at radio hits. 'Can't Stop Partying' features Lil Wayne.

tracks.title: (If You're Wondering If I Want You To) I Want You To
I Don't Want to Let You Go

name: Hurley
teaser: 2010 Weezer's eighth album is a back-to-basics record: 'Memories', 'Ruling Me', and 'Unspoken' are simple, punchy rock. The album's cover features actor Jorge Garcia of Lost. It was a modest success after the pop experiments.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the simplicity — the album was recorded quickly with a rock band feel. 'Memories' is about looking back at the band's past.

name: Everything Will Be Alright in the End
teaser: 2014 Weezer's ninth album was a return to their classic sound: 'Back to the Shack', 'Da Vinci', and 'The British Are Coming' are power-pop anthems. The album was produced by Ric Ocasek, who made their debut. It is considered their best modern record.

exploreAction.targetName: Everything Will Be Alright in the End (2014) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Ocasek's return gave the album the sound of their debut. 'Back to the Shack' is an apology to fans.

tracks.title: I've Had It Up to Here
The Futurescope Trilogy" *I. "The Wasteland" *II. "Anonymous" *III. "Return to Ithaka

name: Pacific Daydream
teaser: 2017 Weezer's tenth album is their most pop: 'Feels Like Summer', 'Mexican Fender', and 'Beach Boys' blend surf pop with modern production. The album was a deliberate radio move. It divided their core fans.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the surf pop — the album was inspired by California summer music. 'Feels Like Summer' was a moderate radio hit.

name: Van Weezer
teaser: 2021 Weezer's album of arena rock: 'The End of the Game', 'Hero', and 'Beginning of the End' are anthemic guitar rock in the style of Van Halen. The album was delayed by the pandemic. It is their heaviest modern work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitar solos — the album was designed as a tribute to 80s arena rock. 'Hero' was used in a Bill & Ted film.

name: OK Human
teaser: 2021 Weezer's orchestral album: 'All My Favorite Songs', 'Grapes of Wrath', and 'Playing My Piano' pair power pop with a full orchestra. The album was recorded with strings and a choir. It is their most unusual work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the strings — the album was recorded entirely with a live orchestra. 'All My Favorite Songs' is about trying to stay positive.

name: Relayer
teaser: 1974 Yes's seventh album replaced Rick Wakeman with Swiss keyboardist Patrick Moraz: 'The Gates of Delirium' is a 22-minute epic about war, and 'Sound Chaser' and 'To Be Over' complete the trio of long pieces. The album's jazz-fusion textures made it their most adventurous work. It reached number five in the UK.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'The Gates of Delirium' — the battle section builds to chaos before resolving into a peaceful coda. Moraz's keyboards give the album a distinct voice.

name: Tales from Topographic Oceans
teaser: 1973 Yes's double album of four side-long suites: 'The Revealing Science of God', 'The Remembering', 'The Ancient', and 'Ritual' are dense, mystical, and controversial. The band's ambition divided critics and fans. It reached number one in the UK.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the themes — each suite explores a text from Indian scripture. The album rewards patient, full-length listens.

tracks.title: The Revealing Science of God (Dance of the Dawn)

name: Going for the One
teaser: 1977 Yes's return to shorter songs and Rick Wakeman: 'Going for the One', 'Wonderous Stories', and 'Awaken' blend pop accessibility with prog ambition. The album was recorded in Switzerland. 'Awaken' is considered one of their greatest pieces.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Awaken' — the 15-minute closer weaves organ, choir, and guitar into a cathedral of sound. The album marked their commercial comeback.

name: Tormato
teaser: 1978 Yes's ninth album divided the band: 'Don't Kill the Whale', 'Madrigal', and 'Release, Release' are lighter and poppier. The album's production was controversial. It was the last with the classic lineup until 1983.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the blend — the album mixes prog structures with pop hooks. 'Don't Kill the Whale' became a minor hit.

tracks.title: On the Silent Wings of Freedom

teaser: 1983 Yes's commercial rebirth: 'Owner of a Lonely Heart', 'Leave It', and 'It Can Happen' are synth-pop hits that reached number one. The album was recorded by a new lineup called Cinema before the Yes name returned. It sold 6 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Trevor Horn's electronic sound defined the album. 'Owner of a Lonely Heart' became their only US number-one single.

name: Big Generator
teaser: 1987 Yes's follow-up to 90125: 'Love Will Find a Way', 'Rhythm of Love', and the title track continue their pop-prog sound. The album was recorded with producer Trevor Horn again. It reached number 15 in the US.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album polishes the electronic sound of 90125. 'Love Will Find a Way' was a minor hit.

name: Union
teaser: 1991 Yes's reunion album combined two factions of the band: 'Lift Me Up', 'Saving My Heart', and 'Miracle of Life' feature eight members. The album was assembled from separate recordings. It sold a million copies and reached number 15 in the US.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the lineup — the album mixes the classic era with the 80s members. 'Lift Me Up' became a rock radio hit.

tracks.title: Without Hope You Cannot Start the Day
The More We Live – Let Go
Dangerous (Look in the Light of What You're Searching For)
Take the Water to the Mountain

name: The Ladder
teaser: 1999 Yes's return to band-based recording: 'Homeworld', 'If Only You Knew', and 'The Messenger' are melodic and organic. The album was recorded live in the studio after years of producer-driven work. It is their most cohesive album of the 90s.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the band interplay — the album was recorded in a mansion with the whole group playing together. 'Homeworld' was written for a video game.

tracks.title: It Will Be a Good Day (The River)

name: Magnification
teaser: 2001 Yes's album with a full orchestra: 'Magnification', 'In the Presence Of', and 'Give Love Each Day' pair the band with 60 musicians. The album was a response to losing their keyboardist. It is their most orchestral work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the orchestra — the strings and brass replace the keyboards throughout. The album rewards a full listen.

tracks.title: In the Presence Of" / I. "Deeper" / II. "Death of Ego" / III. "True Beginner" / IV. "Turn Around and Remember

name: Fly from Here
teaser: 2011 Yes's album produced by Trevor Horn: 'Fly from Here', 'The Man You Always Wanted Me to Be', and 'Hour of Need' blend classic and modern Yes sounds. The title suite was written with Horn in the 80s. It is their first album with new singer Benoit David.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title suite — the 24-minute epic bookends the album. The production is clean and detailed.

tracks.title: Fly from Here, Pt. I: We Can Fly
Fly from Here, Pt. II: Sad Night at the Airfield
Fly from Here, Pt. III: Madman at the Screens
Fly from Here, Pt. IV: Bumpy Ride

The Man You Always Wanted Me to Be

name: Heaven & Earth
teaser: 2014 Yes's 21st album with singer Jon Davison: 'Believe Again', 'The Game', and 'Step Beyond' are melodic and gentle. The album was their last with bassist Chris Squire before his death. It is a bittersweet farewell.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the melodies — the album is warmer than their previous work. 'The Game' has a singable chorus.

tracks.title: In a World of Our Own

name: In the Wake of Poseidon
teaser: 1970 King Crimson's second album continued their debut's dark prog: 'Pictures of a City', 'Cadence and Cascade', and the title track are symphonic and ominous. The album was recorded quickly after lineup changes. It reached number four in the UK.

exploreAction.targetName: In the Wake of Poseidon (1970) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the echoes of their debut — the album revisits similar structures with new twists. The title track's vocal section is haunting.

name: Lizard
teaser: 1970 King Crimson's third album is their most experimental: 'Lizard', 'Indoor Games', and 'Happy Family' blend jazz, classical, and avant-garde sounds. The album features guest vocals and a full brass section. It is their most divisive early work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the jazz — the album's brass arrangements were contributed by Keith Tippett. The title suite is a 23-minute epic about a lizard king.

name: Islands
teaser: 1971 King Crimson's fourth album is their most melodic: 'Islands', 'Formentera Lady', and 'Sailor's Tale' are lyrical and atmospheric. The album featured a full orchestra on the title track. It was the last with the original lineup.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — the orchestral arrangement is among the most beautiful in prog. 'Sailor's Tale' features a searing guitar solo.

name: Larks' Tongues in Aspic
teaser: 1973 King Crimson's fifth album reinvented the band: 'Larks' Tongues in Aspic, Part One', 'Exiles', and 'The Talking Drum' are dark, percussive, and angular. The new lineup included violinist David Cross. It is the beginning of their heaviest era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the percussion — drummer Bill Bruford and percussionist Jamie Muir create a unique rhythmic world. The title piece is a masterpiece of tension.

tracks.title: Larks' Tongues in Aspic, Part One
Larks' Tongues in Aspic, Part Two

name: Starless and Bible Black
teaser: 1974 King Crimson's sixth album: 'The Great Deceiver', 'Fracture', and the title track are improvised and composed in equal measure. The album was assembled from live recordings. 'Fracture' is one of Robert Fripp's greatest compositions.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Fracture' — the 11-minute piece is a guitar tour de force. The album's improvisations reward attention.

name: Discipline
teaser: 1981 King Crimson's return after seven years: 'Frame by Frame', 'Thela Hun Ginjeet', and 'Discipline' are built on interlocking guitar patterns. The new lineup with Adrian Belew and Tony Levin created a totally new sound. It is the beginning of their 80s era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitars — Fripp and Belew weave intricate counterpoint throughout. 'Thela Hun Ginjeet' uses recorded street sounds in its chorus.

name: Beat
teaser: 1982 King Crimson's ninth album continues their 80s sound: 'Neal and Jack and Me', 'Heartbeat', and 'Waiting Man' are rhythmic and pop-adjacent. The album used the same guitar-bass-drum quartet. It is their most accessible 80s work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the rhythm section — Tony Levin's Chapman Stick and Bill Bruford's electronic drums define the sound. The songs are tighter than Discipline.

name: Three of a Perfect Pair
teaser: 1984 King Crimson's tenth album completes their 80s trilogy: 'Three of a Perfect Pair', 'Model Man', and 'Sleepless' blend pop songs with instrumental experiments. The album was their last for a decade. It is the most varied of the trilogy.

exploreAction.targetName: Three of a Perfect Pair (1984) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the split — the album's first half is song-based, the second half is instrumental. 'Sleepless' features danceable electronics.

tracks.title: Nuages (That Which Passes, Passes Like Clouds)

name: THRAK
teaser: 1995 King Crimson's double-trio album: 'THRAK', 'Dinosaur', and 'VROOOM' are heavy, complex, and rhythmic. The lineup featured two bassists and two drummers. The album is the sound of the band at maximum power.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the twin drummers — Bruford and Pat Mastelotto create a massive rhythmic force. The album's title track is a relentless machine.

name: The ConstruKction of Light
teaser: 2000 King Crimson's twelfth album is their most abrasive: 'The ConstruKction of Light', 'ProzaKc Blues', and 'FraKctured' are dense and dissonant. The album divided fans. It is their most experimental work of the modern era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the complexity — the album's rhythms and harmonies are among the most intricate in rock. It rewards repeated listens.

tracks.title: The World's My Oyster Soup Kitchen Floor Wax Museum
Larks' Tongues in Aspic – Part IV

name: The Power to Believe
teaser: 2003 King Crimson's thirteenth and final studio album: 'The Power to Believe', 'Level Five', and 'Happy with What You Have to Be Happy With' return to their heavy sound. The album features spoken samples and dense riffing. It is a fitting finale.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the themes — the album's lyrics and samples explore faith and doubt. 'Level Five' is a ferocious instrumental.

tracks.title: The Power to Believe I: A Cappella
Happy with What You Have to Be Happy With
The Power to Believe IV: Coda

name: Aqualung
teaser: 1971 Jethro Tull's breakthrough concept album: 'Aqualung', 'Cross-Eyed Mary', and 'Locomotive Breath' are flute-driven rock songs about faith and hypocrisy. The album sold 7 million copies. It defined the band's sound.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the flute — Ian Anderson's playing is the album's signature. The title track's heavy riff was a departure for the band.

tracks.title: Excerpts from the Ian Anderson Interview
Life is a Long Song promotional video

name: Thick as a Brick
teaser: 1972 Jethro Tull's single 44-minute song split across two sides: 'Thick as a Brick' tells a sprawling story inspired by a fictional schoolboy's epic poem. The album reached number one in the US. It is the definitive prog concept album.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the continuity — the album is one continuous piece with recurring themes. The lyrics are a parody of epic poetry.

tracks.title: Thick as a Brick, Part One
Thick as a Brick, Part Two

name: A Passion Play
teaser: 1973 Jethro Tull's follow-up concept album: 'A Passion Play' continues the single-song format with a story about a man's afterlife. The album was divisive, with critics and fans split. It reached number one in the UK.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the narrative — the album follows its protagonist through judgment and rebirth. The band defended it fiercely.

tracks.title: The Story of the Hare Who Lost His Spectacles

name: War Child
teaser: 1974 Jethro Tull's album of songs written for an unmade film: 'Bungle in the Jungle', 'Skating Away on the Thin Ice of the New Day', and 'Only Solitaire' are melodic and theatrical. The album sold a million copies. It is their most accessible of the 70s.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the melodies — the album's songs are catchier than their concept epics. 'Bungle in the Jungle' became their biggest US hit.

tracks.title: Skating Away on the Thin Ice of the New Day

name: Minstrel in the Gallery
teaser: 1975 Jethro Tull's return to harder rock: 'Minstrel in the Gallery', 'Cold Wind to Valhalla', and 'Baker St. Muse' are long, acoustic, and electric. The album was recorded on tour. It is their most personal work of the decade.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the dynamics — the album swings between delicate acoustic passages and heavy riffs. 'Baker St. Muse' is a 17-minute suite.

name: Too Old to Rock 'n' Roll: Too Young to Die!
teaser: 1976 Jethro Tull's concept album about an aging rocker: 'Too Old to Rock 'n' Roll', 'Rocks on the Road', and 'The Whistler' are bittersweet and melodic. The album was based on a comic strip. It is their most humorous work.

exploreAction.targetName: Too Old to Rock 'n' Roll: Too Young to Die! (1976) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the story — the album follows its hero from the 50s to the present. 'The Whistler' became a live favorite.

tracks.title: From a Dead Beat to an Old Greaser
Too Old to Rock 'n' Roll: Too Young to Die

name: Songs from the Wood
teaser: 1977 Jethro Tull's folk-rock masterpiece: 'Songs from the Wood', 'The Whistler', and 'Ring Out, Solstice Bells' are warm, pastoral, and English. The album marked their turn from prog to folk. It is considered one of their best.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the harmonies — the album's vocal arrangements are the band's richest. The title track celebrates rural England.

name: Heavy Horses
teaser: 1978 Jethro Tull's second folk-rock album: 'Heavy Horses', 'Moths', and 'Rover' continue their pastoral turn. The title track is a tribute to working horses. The album is the quieter sequel to Songs from the Wood.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the acoustic textures — the album is built on mandolin, flute, and string quartets. 'Moths' is one of their most beautiful songs.

name: Stormwatch
teaser: 1979 Jethro Tull's final album with the classic lineup: 'North Sea Oil', 'Orion', and 'Dun Ringill' are folk-rock songs about the sea and land. The album was recorded as the band was falling apart. It closes their folk era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the themes — the songs are about ecology and the elements. The album rewards a full listen.

name: Broadsword and the Beast
teaser: 1982 Jethro Tull's synth-heavy album: 'Broadsword', 'Beastie', and 'Flying Dutchman' blend folk themes with 80s electronics. The album reached number 27 in the US. It is their most distinctive album of the decade.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album's synthesizers date it to the 80s but the melodies endure. 'Broadsword' is a powerful opener.

name: Under Wraps
teaser: 1984 Jethro Tull's electronic album: 'Lap of Luxury', 'Under Wraps', and 'Nobody's Car' use drum machines and synths almost exclusively. The album damaged Ian Anderson's voice from strained delivery. It is their most controversial work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the experiment — the album abandoned guitars and flute for electronics. It is a curiosity in their catalog.

name: Crest of a Knave
teaser: 1987 Jethro Tull's comeback album: 'Farm on the Freeway', 'Steel Monkey', and 'Said She Was a Dancer' are blues-rock songs that won the Grammy for Best Hard Rock/Metal Performance, beating Metallica. The album sold 3 million copies. It is their biggest hit of the decade.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the blues — the album is heavier and more straightforward than their 70s work. The Grammy controversy made it famous.

name: Rock Island
teaser: 1989 Jethro Tull's album of cynical rock songs: 'Kissing Willie', 'Rock Island', and 'Big Riff and Mando' are bluesy and humorous. The album's cover was censored. It is a minor entry in their catalog.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitar — Martin Barre's playing is the album's highlight. The songs are more straightforward than their prog work.

name: Catfish Rising
teaser: 1991 Jethro Tull's blues-rock album: 'Rocks on the Road', 'Still Loving You Tonight', and 'Doctor to My Disease' return to a live band sound. The album was recorded with a smaller lineup. It is a return to basics.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the blues — the album is rooted in American blues forms. The band plays together throughout.

tracks.title: Gold-Tipped Boots, Black Jacket and Tie

name: Roots to Branches
teaser: 1995 Jethro Tull's world-music album: 'Roots to Branches', 'Rare and Precious Chain', and 'Another Harry's Bar' blend folk, rock, and Eastern influences. The album was their first studio work in four years. It is their most adventurous late work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the exotic scales — the album uses Indian-influenced melodies. The title track is a strong opener.

name: J-Tull Dot Com
teaser: 1999 Jethro Tull's album exploring the internet age: 'Dot Com', 'Hot Mango Flush', and 'Hunt by Numbers' are folk-rock songs about technology. The album was recorded with a keyboardist. It is a modest late entry.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the themes — the album's lyrics comment on the digital age. 'Hot Mango Flush' is a playful highlight.

name: The Jethro Tull Christmas Album
teaser: 2003 Jethro Tull's holiday collection: 'Birthday Card at Christmas', 'Holly Herald', and re-recordings of 'A Christmas Song' blend carols with the band's folk-rock. The album was a surprise hit. It is a warm seasonal entry.

exploreAction.targetName: The Jethro Tull Christmas Album (2003) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the carols — the band reworks traditional tunes with flute and mandolin. The album is a fan favorite at the holidays.

tracks.title: Jack Frost and the Hooded Crow

name: The Zealot Gene
teaser: 2022 Jethro Tull's first studio album in 19 years: 'The Zealot Gene', 'Shoshana Sleeping', and 'Mine Is the Mountain' are song-based folk-rock with biblical themes. The album was written over a decade. It was a successful return.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the songcraft — the album trades epics for concise songs. 'The Zealot Gene' is a strong title track.

name: RökFlöte
teaser: 2023 Jethro Tull's Norse-themed album: 'Voluspo', 'Ginnungagap', and 'Hammer on Hammer' explore Norse mythology with folk rock. The album was a critical success. It is their most ambitious modern work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the themes — each song explores a Norse myth. The album's production is rich and detailed.

name: Movement
teaser: 1981 New Order's debut continued Joy Division's sound: 'Dreams Never End', 'Truth', and 'ICB' are dark, rhythmic, and transitional. The album was recorded as the band mourned Ian Curtis. It is the bridge to their electronic era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the transition — the album mixes post-punk guitars with early synthesizers. 'Dreams Never End' hints at their dance future.

name: Low-Life
teaser: 1985 New Order's fifth album is their most human: 'Love Vigilantes', 'The Perfect Kiss', and 'Sub-culture' blend electronics with warmth. The album was recorded in their new studio. It is a fan favorite.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album was recorded at home with new equipment. 'The Perfect Kiss' became a club anthem.

name: Brotherhood
teaser: 1986 New Order's album split between dance tracks and guitar songs: 'Bizarre Love Triangle', 'All Day Long', and 'Every Little Counts' balance both sides. The album reached number nine in the UK. 'Bizarre Love Triangle' is a dance classic.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the split — the first half is electronic, the second half is guitar-based. 'Bizarre Love Triangle' remains their most beloved song.

tracks.title: As It Is When It Was

name: Technique
teaser: 1989 New Order's acid house album: 'Fine Time', 'Round & Round', and 'Vanishing Point' are Ibiza-influenced dance music. The album was recorded between nights out in Ibiza. It reached number one in the UK.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the acid house — the album embraces the late-80s rave sound. 'Fine Time' has a spoken-word intro over a pumping groove.

name: Republic
teaser: 1993 New Order's electronic peak: 'Regret', 'World in Motion', and 'Ruined in a Day' are polished dance-pop. The album was their biggest commercial success in the US. It is their last album for a decade.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album was recorded in the wake of their label's bankruptcy. 'Regret' became a global hit.

name: Get Ready
teaser: 2001 New Order's return with rock guitars: 'Crystal', '60 Miles an Hour', and 'Someone Like You' blend their dance history with a live band. The album was produced by Steve Osborne. It is their most guitar-heavy album since the 80s.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitars — the album was a deliberate return to rock. 'Crystal' is a soaring opener.

name: Waiting for the Sirens' Call
teaser: 2005 New Order's album of return: 'Krafty', 'Waiting for the Sirens' Call', and 'Jetstream' are polished synth-pop. The album was their last with bassist Peter Hook. It is a bittersweet finale to their classic era.

exploreAction.targetName: Waiting for the Sirens' Call (2005) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the melodies — the album's hooks are as strong as their classics. 'Krafty' is a warm, nostalgic single.

name: Lost Sirens
teaser: 2013 New Order's collection of outtakes from their 2005 sessions: 'I'll Stay with You', 'Hellbent', and 'Sugarcane' are polished leftovers. The album was released without Peter Hook's involvement. It is a minor but welcome entry.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the outtakes — the songs were recorded for the previous album but left off. 'Hellbent' is a danceable highlight.

name: Music Complete
teaser: 2015 New Order's return after a decade: 'Restless', 'Plastic', and 'Tutti Frutti' are their most electronic album since Technique. The album features guests like Iggy Pop and La Roux. It is a strong late-career statement.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album embraces disco and house sounds. 'Tutti Frutti' with La Roux is a highlight.

name: Vol. 2... Hard Knock Life
teaser: 1998 Jay-Z's commercial breakthrough: 'Hard Knock Life (Ghetto Anthem)', 'Money, Cash, Hoes', and 'Can I Get A...' made him a superstar. The album sampled the musical Annie for its title track. It sold 5 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the crossover — the album balanced street credibility with pop hooks. 'Hard Knock Life' became an unlikely anthem.

name: Vol. 3... Life and Times of S. Carter
teaser: 1999 Jay-Z's fourth album: 'Big Pimpin'', 'Jigga My Nigga', and 'Things That U Do' are brash and funky. The album was a response to his legal troubles. It is a transitional work between his eras.

exploreAction.targetName: Vol. 3... Life and Times of S. Carter (1999) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Timbaland and Swizz Beatz contribute distinctive beats. 'Big Pimpin'' became a summer anthem.

tracks.title: Do It Again (Put Ya Hands Up)
Hova Song (Outro)" / "Jigga My Nigga" / "Girl's Best Friend

name: The Dynasty: Roc La Familia
teaser: 2000 Jay-Z's album credited to Roc-A-Fella Records: 'I Just Wanna Love U (Give It 2 Me)', 'The R.O.C.', and 'Change the Game' showcase his label's roster. The album was recorded in two weeks. It is a celebration of his empire.

exploreAction.targetName: The Dynasty: Roc La Familia (2000) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the label showcase — the album features Beanie Sigel, Memphis Bleek, and others. 'I Just Wanna Love U' became a hit.

tracks.title: I Just Wanna Love U (Give It 2 Me)

name: The Blueprint 2: The Gift & The Curse
teaser: 2002 Jay-Z's double album: 'Excuse Me Miss', '03 Bonnie & Clyde', and 'Hovi Baby' are sprawling and ambitious. The album sold 3 million copies. It is a mixed bag but contains gems.

exploreAction.targetName: The Blueprint 2: The Gift & The Curse (2002) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the range — the double album spans pop hits and dense street tracks. '03 Bonnie & Clyde' with Beyoncé was a hit.

tracks.title: A Ballad for the Fallen Soldier
What They Gonna Do, Part II

name: The Black Album
teaser: 2003 Jay-Z's 'retirement' album: '99 Problems', 'Dirt off Your Shoulder', and 'Encore' are a victory lap. Each track had a different producer, from Kanye West to Rick Rubin. It sold 4 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production variety — every song sounds distinct. '99 Problems' with Rick Rubin is a hard-rock rap classic.

name: Kingdom Come
teaser: 2006 Jay-Z's comeback album: 'Show Me What You Got', 'Lost One', and '30 Something' address his return to rap. The album was criticized for being out of touch. It still debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the maturity — the album reflects on his success and age. 'Lost One' is a poignant tribute to a fallen friend.

name: American Gangster
teaser: 2007 Jay-Z's concept album inspired by the film: 'Blue Magic', 'Roc Boys (And the Winner Is)...', and 'American Dreamin'' are cinematic street sagas. The album was produced in the spirit of 70s soul. It is his strongest work of the decade.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the concept — the album follows a drug dealer's rise and fall. The soul samples give it a vintage feel.

name: Magna Carta Holy Grail
teaser: 2013 Jay-Z's album of luxury and legacy: 'Holy Grail', 'Picasso Baby', and 'Tom Ford' are grandiose and introspective. The album was released through a Samsung app partnership. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guest list — Justin Timberlake, Beyoncé, and Rick Ross appear. 'Holy Grail' samples Nirvana's 'Smells Like Teen Spirit'.

teaser: 2017 Jay-Z's confessional album: '4:44', 'The Story of O.J.', and 'Family Feud' address infidelity, race, and family. The album was released exclusively to Tidal first. It is his most personal work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the honesty — the title track is an apology to Beyoncé. The album's production is sparse and soulful.

name: Infinite
teaser: 1996 Eminem's independent debut: 'Infinite', 'Backstabber', and 'Open Mic' show a young rapper finding his voice. The album sold poorly but caught the attention of Dr. Dre. It is a fascinating origin story.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the evolution — the album shows Em before his Slim Shady persona. 'Infinite' is a showcase of early technical skill.

name: Encore
teaser: 2004 Eminem's fifth album: 'Just Lose It', 'Mockingbird', and 'Like Toy Soldiers' mix humor, heart, and rage. The album was recorded during his addiction struggles. It is a troubled but revealing work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the emotional tracks — 'Mockingbird' is a song to his daughter, 'Like Toy Soldiers' addresses his feuds. The album's darker songs outshine the comedy.

name: Relapse
teaser: 2009 Eminem's comeback after his overdose: 'Crack a Bottle', 'Beautiful', and '3 a.m.' are dark, technical, and horror-themed. The album was produced almost entirely by Dr. Dre. It won a Grammy for Best Rap Album.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the technical skill — the album showcases Em's best rapping in years. 'Beautiful' is a reflective highlight.

name: Recovery
teaser: 2010 Eminem's album of sobriety: 'Not Afraid', 'Love the Way You Lie', and 'No Love' are anthems of survival. The album sold 20 million copies. It is his most commercially successful work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the message — the album is about rebuilding after addiction. 'Love the Way You Lie' with Rihanna was a global smash.

name: The Marshall Mathers LP 2
teaser: 2013 Eminem's sequel to his masterpiece: 'Berzerk', 'Rap God', and 'Headlights' revisit his legacy. The album's 12-minute 'Rap God' became famous for its speed. It won a Grammy for Best Rap Album.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the references — the album revisits themes and samples from the original. 'Headlights' is a reconciliation with his mother.

name: Revival
teaser: 2017 Eminem's political album: 'Walk on Water', 'River', and 'Untouchable' address race, politics, and his critics. The album received mixed reviews. It is his most contentious work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the politics — the album was released during the Trump era. 'Untouchable' addresses racial profiling.

name: Kamikaze
teaser: 2018 Eminem's surprise diss album: 'The Ringer', 'Lucky You', and 'Fall' attack critics and fellow rappers. The album was released without announcement. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the aggression — the album is a response to criticism of Revival. 'The Ringer' is a relentless opener.

name: Music to Be Murdered By
teaser: 2020 Eminem's album with Alfred Hitchcock samples: 'Godzilla', 'Darkness', and 'Premonition' are technical and dark. The album debuted at number one. 'Godzilla' features a legendary rapid-fire verse.

exploreAction.targetName: Music to Be Murdered By (2020) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the wordplay — the album is packed with dense, rapid rhymes. 'Darkness' addresses the Las Vegas shooting with a twist.

name: The Death of Slim Shady (Coup de Grâce)
teaser: 2024 Eminem's conceptual farewell to his alter ego: 'Houdini', 'Tobey', and 'Renaissance' kill off Slim Shady in a narrative album. The album debuted at number one. It is his most ambitious late work.

exploreAction.targetName: The Death of Slim Shady (Coup de Grâce) (2024) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the concept — the album is structured as a story about destroying his persona. 'Houdini' became a global hit.

name: N.W.A and the Posse
teaser: 1987 N.W.A's early compilation: 'Boyz-n-the-Hood', 'Dopeman', and '8 Ball' collect early tracks by Ice Cube and Eazy-E. The album predates the group's official debut. It is a rough sketch of what came next.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the origins — the compilation shows the group before their breakthrough. 'Boyz-n-the-Hood' was an early hit.

tracks.title: Tuffest Man Alive featuring The D.O.C.

name: Efil4zaggin
teaser: 1991 N.W.A's second and final album: 'Alwayz into Somethin'', 'Appetite for Destruction', and 'Findum, Fuckum & Flee' are raw and confrontational. The album was recorded without Ice Cube. It reached number one, a first for gangsta rap.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Dr. Dre's beats are more polished than the debut. The album's lyrics are among the most explicit ever released.

name: The Predator
teaser: 1992 Ice Cube's third album: 'It Was a Good Day', 'Check Yo Self', and 'Today Was a Good Day' are West Coast classics. The album was recorded after the LA riots. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the mood — the album blends anger and reflection. 'It Was a Good Day' is one of the most beloved hip-hop songs ever.

tracks.title: We Had to Tear This Mothafucka Up
Say Hi to the Bad Guy

name: Lethal Injection
teaser: 1993 Ice Cube's fourth album: 'You Know How We Do It', 'Bop Gun (One Nation)', and 'What Can I Do?' are funkier and more melodic. The album was produced with DJ Pooh. It is his most polished early work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the funk — the album samples Parliament and George Clinton. 'You Know How We Do It' is a laid-back classic.

tracks.title: You Know How We Do It
Make It Ruff, Make It Smooth

name: The Great Adventures of Slick Rick
teaser: 1988 Slick Rick's debut is a storytelling masterpiece: 'Children's Story', 'Hey Young World', and 'Mona Lisa' are witty, detailed, and influential. The album is one of the greatest debuts in hip-hop. It defined narrative rap.

exploreAction.targetName: The Great Adventures of Slick Rick (1988) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the stories — every track is a miniature narrative. 'Children's Story' was covered and sampled countless times.

name: De La Soul Is Dead
teaser: 1991 De La Soul's dark sequel to their debut: 'A Roller Skating Jam Named 'Saturdays'', 'Ring Ring Ring (Ha Ha Hey)', and 'Millie Pulled a Pistol on Santa' are moody and eclectic. The album rejected their image. It is a bold, strange classic.

exploreAction.targetName: De La Soul Is Dead (1991) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the skits — the album is framed as a continuous radio broadcast. 'Millie Pulled a Pistol on Santa' is a shocking narrative.

tracks.title: Johnny's Dead AKA Vincent Mason (Live from the BK Lounge)
Afro Connections at a Hi 5 (In the Eyes of the Hoodlum)
Millie Pulled a Pistol on Santa
Not Over till the Fat Lady Plays the Demo

name: Buhloone Mindstate
teaser: 1993 De La Soul's jazz-influenced album: 'Ego Trippin' (Part Two)', 'I Am I Be', and 'Patti Dooke' are loose, live, and philosophical. The album was recorded with jazz musicians. It is their most organic work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the live instruments — the album features a horn section and Maceo Parker. 'I Am I Be' is a statement of identity.

name: Stakes Is High
teaser: 1996 De La Soul's album of independence: 'Stakes Is High', 'The Bizness', and 'Itzsoweezee (Hot)' are sample-dense and politically aware. The album was a response to commercial rap. It is their most critically acclaimed later work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — J Dilla contributed beats, including 'Stakes Is High'. The album's title track is a landmark.

tracks.title: Baby Baby Baby Baby Ooh Baby

name: The Grind Date
teaser: 2004 De La Soul's album of maturity: 'Shopping Bags (She Got from You)', 'Church', and 'Much More' are polished and reflective. The album reunited them with producer 9th Wonder. It is their strongest album of the 2000s.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — 9th Wonder and Madlib contribute beats. 'Shopping Bags' is a fan favorite.

name: and the Anonymous Nobody...
teaser: 2016 De La Soul's crowdfunded album: 'Pain', 'Drawn', and 'Property of Spitkool.com' were built from live improvisations. The album was funded by fans on Kickstarter. It is their final album before their catalog hit streaming.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the process — the album was built from jam sessions with live musicians. 'Pain' features a spoken-word intro.

name: The Impossible Kid
teaser: 2016 Aesop Rock's solo album: 'Rings', 'Kirby', and 'Lotta Years' are dense, witty, and personal. The album was recorded alone at home. It is his most accessible work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the wordplay — Aesop's dense rhymes reward repeated listens. 'Rings' is about his failed art career.

name: Because the Internet
teaser: 2013 Childish Gambino's concept album: '3005', 'Sweatpants', and 'Flight of the Navigator' explore loneliness and internet culture. The album was accompanied by a 72-page screenplay. It is his breakthrough work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the narrative — the album follows a character through isolation. '3005' is a trap-pop classic.

tracks.title: Playing Around Before the Party Starts
II. Earth: The Oldest Computer (The Last Night)
III. Life: The Biggest Troll (Andrew Auernheimer)

name: Awaken, My Love!
teaser: 2016 Childish Gambino's funk album: 'Redbone', 'Me and Your Mama', and 'Terrified' are psychedelic soul. The album abandoned rapping for singing. 'Redbone' became a Grammy-winning classic.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the funk — the album channels Parliament-Funkadelic. 'Redbone' has one of the most sampled vocals of the decade.

tracks.title: The Night Me and Your Mama Met

teaser: 2020 Childish Gambino's surprise album: 'Algorhythm', 'This Is America', and 'Time' are experimental and political. The album was released as a stream with a digital artwork. 'This Is America' had won the Grammy for Record of the Year.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the experimentation — the album blends funk, gospel, and electronic music. 'Algorhythm' is a dense opener.

name: Camp
teaser: 2011 Childish Gambino's major-label debut: 'Bonfire', 'Heartbeat', and 'Backpackers' are witty, pop-aware rap. The album was produced largely by Ludwig Goransson. It is his most direct work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Ludwig Goransson's beats are cinematic. 'Bonfire' is a brash statement of arrival.

name: Richard D. James Album
teaser: 1996 Aphex Twin's breakthrough: 'Cornish Acid', '4', and 'Girl/Boy Song' blend drill-and-bass rhythms with classical strings. The album was recorded at his home studio. It is his most melodic work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the drum programming — the beats are impossibly fast and precise. 'Girl/Boy Song' has a beautiful string section.

name: Drukqs
teaser: 2001 Aphex Twin's double album: 'Vordhosbn', 'Avril 14th', and 'Mt Saint Michel' alternate between frenetic drill-and-bass and delicate piano. The album was recorded over years. It is his most ambitious work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the contrast — the album swings between chaos and calm. 'Avril 14th' is one of his most beloved piano pieces.

tracks.title: Mt Saint Michel + Saint Michaels Mount

name: Syro
teaser: 2014 Aphex Twin's return after 13 years: 'Xmas_Evet10', 'minipops 67', and 'Aisatsana' are warm and playful. The album was announced with a blimp over London. It won a Grammy for Best Dance/Electronic Album.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the warmth — the album is more melodic than his abrasive work. It is a fitting comeback.

name: Geogaddi
teaser: 2002 Boards of Canada's darker follow-up: 'Music Is Math', '1969', and 'The Beach at Redpoint' are eerie, detailed, and occult. The album was rumored to contain hidden messages. It is their most mysterious work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the details — the album is dense with samples and hidden sounds. It rewards repeated, careful listening.

tracks.title: The Devil Is in the Details
A Is to B as B Is to C

name: The Campfire Headphase
teaser: 2005 Boards of Canada's album with guitars: 'Dayvan Cowboy', 'Peacock Tail', and 'Chromakey Dreamcoat' blend their electronic sound with folk guitar. The album was a departure for the duo. It is their warmest work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitars — the album was the first to feature live instruments prominently. 'Dayvan Cowboy' is a highlight.

name: Tomorrow's Harvest
teaser: 2013 Boards of Canada's dystopian album: 'Reach for the Dead', 'Nothing Is Real', and 'Jacquard Causeway' are bleak, cinematic, and precise. The album was teased with a code hidden in vinyl grooves. It is their most political work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the mood — the album imagines a post-collapse world. It rewards headphones and patience.

name: In a Beautiful Place Out in the Country
teaser: 2000 Boards of Canada's EP: 'Amo Bishop Roden', 'Kid for Today', and the title track are gentle and hypnotic. The EP was named after a Branch Davidian settlement. It is their most focused release.

exploreAction.targetName: In a Beautiful Place Out in the Country (2000) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — its simple melody is one of their most memorable. The EP is a perfect entry point.

tracks.title: In a Beautiful Place Out in the Country

name: Thrust
teaser: 1974 Herbie Hancock's follow-up to Head Hunters: 'Actual Proof', 'Palm Grease', and 'Spank-a-Lee' are deep, funky, and complex. The album featured a new lineup. It is a fan favorite among jazz-funk fans.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the interplay — the band locks into complex grooves. 'Actual Proof' is a fusion classic.

name: Romantic Warrior
teaser: 1976 Return to Forever's fusion masterpiece: 'Medieval Overture', 'Sorceress', and 'The Romantic Warrior' are classically influenced jazz-rock. The album is the peak of 70s fusion. It remains a touchstone for guitarists and bassists.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the virtuosity — the band plays with incredible precision and speed. The album is a gateway to jazz fusion.

tracks.title: Duel of the Jester and the Tyrant (Parts I and II)

name: Hymn of the Seventh Galaxy
teaser: 1973 Return to Forever's electric debut: 'Hymn of the Seventh Galaxy', 'After the Cosmic Rain', and 'Space Circus' are cosmic fusion. The album marked the band's turn from acoustic to electric. It is a fusion landmark.

exploreAction.targetName: Hymn of the Seventh Galaxy (1973) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the energy — the album's fast, precise playing defines the genre. 'Space Circus' is a fan favorite.

name: Unchained
teaser: 1996 Johnny Cash's second album with Rick Rubin: 'Rusty Cage', 'Mean Eyed Cat', and 'Country Boy' feature Tom Petty's Heartbreakers. The album's cover showed Cash flipping the camera. It won a Grammy for Best Country Album.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the covers — Cash transforms Soundgarden's 'Rusty Cage' and Beck's 'Rowboat'. The album is a masterclass in reinterpretation.

tracks.title: The One Rose (That's Left in My Heart)

name: Solitary Man
teaser: 2000 Johnny Cash's third album with Rick Rubin: 'Solitary Man', 'I Won't Back Down', and 'The Mercy Seat' are stark and defiant. The album was recorded as his health declined. It is a powerful statement of endurance.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the defiance — Cash covers Neil Diamond and Tom Petty with authority. 'The Mercy Seat' is a Nick Cave cover.

tracks.title: That Lucky Old Sun (Just Rolls Around Heaven All Day)
Would You Lay with Me (In a Field of Stone)

name: The Man Comes Around
teaser: 2002 Johnny Cash's final album: 'Hurt', 'The Man Comes Around', and 'We'll Meet Again' are meditations on mortality. The album was released months before his death. 'Hurt', a Nine Inch Nails cover, became his greatest late performance.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Hurt' — the video and performance turned the song into a farewell. The album is a profound final statement.

tracks.title: First Time Ever I Saw Your Face
I'm So Lonesome I Could Cry

name: Unearthed
teaser: 2003 Johnny Cash's five-disc box set of unreleased American Recordings sessions: 'Long Black Veil', 'The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face', and 'Pocahontas' are raw and intimate. The set includes 60 tracks. It is a treasure trove.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the range — the set covers gospel, country, and rock covers. 'Pocahontas' with Neil Young is a highlight.
