name: American VI: Ain't No Grave
teaser: 2010 Johnny Cash's posthumous final album: 'Ain't No Grave', 'Redemption Day', and '1 Corinthians 15:55' are spiritual and defiant. The album was completed after his death. It is a fitting close to the American series.

exploreAction.targetName: American VI: Ain't No Grave (2010) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the faith — the album's gospel themes close his career. 'Ain't No Grave' is a powerful statement of belief.

tracks.title: Ain't No Grave (Gonna Hold This Body Down)
Can't Help But Wonder Where I'm Bound
Last Night I Had the Strangest Dream

name: I Want You
teaser: 1976 Marvin Gaye's album of longing: 'I Want You', 'After the Dance', and 'Since I Had You' are dreamy, layered, and hypnotic. The album's production by Leon Ware is luxurious. It is his most sensual work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album's arrangements are lush and detailed. 'After the Dance' is a classic.

tracks.title: I Wanna Be Where You Are
Soon I'll Be Loving You Again

name: Here, My Dear
teaser: 1978 Marvin Gaye's double album about his divorce: 'Here, My Dear', 'When Did You Stop Loving Me, When Did I Stop Loving You', and 'Anger' are painful, honest, and sprawling. The album's royalties went to his ex-wife. It is his most personal work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the honesty — the album documents the end of a marriage in real time. It was a commercial failure that became a cult classic.

tracks.title: When Did You Stop Loving Me, When Did I Stop Loving You
When Did You Stop Loving Me, When Did I Stop Loving You (Instrumental)
You Can Leave, But It's Going to Cost You
When Did You Stop Loving Me, When Did I Stop Loving You (Reprise)

name: Midnight Love
teaser: 1982 Marvin Gaye's final album: 'Sexual Healing', 'Midnight Lady', and 'Third World Girl' blend funk, reggae, and electronics. 'Sexual Healing' became his biggest hit and won a Grammy. The album was his comeback before his death.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Sexual Healing' — the song's groove and vocal performance made it an instant classic. The album is a bittersweet final chapter.

name: Fulfillingness' First Finale
teaser: 1974 Stevie Wonder's fourth masterpiece in a row: 'Boogie On Reggae Woman', 'You Haven't Done Nothin'', and 'Heaven Is 10 Zillion Light Years Away' are funky and political. The album won Album of the Year at the Grammys.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the range — the album moves from reggae-funk to gentle ballads. 'You Haven't Done Nothin'' was a protest against Nixon.

tracks.title: Heaven Is 10 Zillion Light Years Away
They Won't Go When I Go

name: Hotter than July
teaser: 1980 Stevie Wonder's most political album: 'Master Blaster (Jammin')', 'Happy Birthday', and 'All I Do' are joyful and committed. 'Happy Birthday' helped make Martin Luther King Jr. Day a national holiday. It is his best-selling album of the 80s.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the politics — the album campaigned for the King holiday. 'Master Blaster' is a reggae tribute to Bob Marley.

tracks.title: Did I Hear You Say You Love Me
I Ain't Gonna Stand for It
As If You Read My Mind

name: Music of My Mind
teaser: 1972 Stevie Wonder's first album of full artistic control: 'Superwoman (Where Were You When I Needed You)', 'I Love Every Little Thing About You', and 'Keep On Running' are experimental and personal. The album marked the beginning of his classic period.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the experimentation — the album was recorded with Wonder playing most instruments. It is the start of his golden run.

tracks.title: Superwoman (Where Were You When I Needed You)
I Love Every Little Thing About You

name: Signed, Sealed & Delivered
teaser: 1970 Stevie Wonder's album with Motown's control loosening: 'Signed, Sealed, Delivered I'm Yours', 'Heaven Help Us All', and 'I Can't Help It' are catchy and heartfelt. The title track became his first pop hit in years. It is his last Motown-controlled album.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — its energy and vocal power made it a classic. The album shows him straining toward independence.

name: For Once in My Life
teaser: 1968 Stevie Wonder's album of covers and originals: 'For Once in My Life', 'Shoo-Be-Doo-Be-Doo-Da-Day', and 'I Don't Know Why' are joyful and funky. The title track became his biggest hit. It is his most consistent album of the 60s.

exploreAction.targetName: For Once in My Life (1968) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the funk — the album's horn arrangements are tight and swinging. 'For Once in My Life' is a Motown classic.

name: Songs from a Room
teaser: 1969 Leonard Cohen's second album: 'Bird on the Wire', 'The Partisan', and 'Story of Isaac' are sparse and powerful. The album was recorded in Nashville. It is darker and more focused than his debut.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the restraint — the album's minimal arrangements let the words carry. 'Bird on the Wire' is one of his greatest songs.

name: New Skin for the Old Ceremony
teaser: 1974 Leonard Cohen's fourth album: 'Chelsea Hotel No. 2', 'Who by Fire', and 'Take This Longing' are intimate and confessional. The album's production added strings and horns. It is his most varied early work.

exploreAction.targetName: New Skin for the Old Ceremony (1974) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the confession — 'Chelsea Hotel No. 2' is about his affair with Janis Joplin. The album rewards attention to the lyrics.

name: I'm Your Man
teaser: 1988 Leonard Cohen's synth-heavy comeback: 'First We Take Manhattan', 'I'm Your Man', and 'Everybody Knows' are witty, dark, and danceable. The album's electronic production surprised fans. It is his most influential late work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the humor — the album's wit cuts through the darkness. 'Everybody Knows' has been covered countless times.

name: The Future
teaser: 1992 Leonard Cohen's apocalyptic album: 'The Future', 'Anthem', and 'Democracy' are grand, prophetic, and dark. The album was written in the shadow of the Gulf War. It is his most political work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the prophecy — the title track predicts a dark future with glee. 'Anthem' contains his famous line about cracks letting in the light.

name: Ten New Songs
teaser: 2001 Leonard Cohen's collaboration with Sharon Robinson: 'In My Secret Life', 'A Thousand Kisses Deep', and 'Boogie Street' are mellow and meditative. The album was written and produced with Robinson over years. It is his warmest late work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the calm — the album's gentle arrangements suit his aged voice. 'In My Secret Life' is a standout.

name: You Want It Darker
teaser: 2016 Leonard Cohen's final album: 'You Want It Darker', 'Treaty', and 'Traveling Light' confront mortality with grace. The album was recorded as he neared death. It is a profound farewell.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the finality — the title track is a direct address to God. The album's choir and strings give it a liturgical feel.

tracks.title: If I Didn't Have Your Love

name: Catch a Fire
teaser: 1973 Bob Marley's international debut: 'Concrete Jungle', 'Stir It Up', and 'Stop That Train' introduced reggae to the world. The album was remixed with overdubs for Western audiences. It is the beginning of Marley's global legend.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the grooves — the album's rhythm section, the Barrett brothers, drives every track. 'Stir It Up' became a hit for Johnny Nash.

tracks.title: Baby We've Got a Date (Rock It Baby)

name: Burnin'
teaser: 1973 The Wailers' second international album: 'I Shot the Sheriff', 'Get Up, Stand Up', and 'Small Axe' are protest anthems. Eric Clapton covered 'I Shot the Sheriff' and made it a global hit. The album is their most political.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the politics — the album's songs demand justice. 'Get Up, Stand Up' was written with Peter Tosh.

name: Natty Dread
teaser: 1974 Bob Marley's first album without Peter Tosh and Bunny Wailer: 'No Woman, No Cry', 'Lively Up Yourself', and 'Them Belly Full' are confident and soulful. The album was recorded with the Wailers band. It is a transitional classic.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — 'No Woman, No Cry' became one of the most loved songs in reggae. The album's groove is relaxed and powerful.

name: Rastaman Vibration
teaser: 1976 Bob Marley's US breakthrough: 'War', 'Roots, Rock, Reggae', and 'Crazy Baldhead' are militant and joyful. The album was his highest-charting US release. It is a statement of faith and resistance.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the message — 'War' adapts a speech by Haile Selassie. The album's title track celebrates reggae's global reach.

name: Kaya
teaser: 1978 Bob Marley's album of love and relaxation: 'Is This Love', 'Satisfy My Soul', and the title track are gentle and romantic. The album was recorded after the assassination attempt on his life. It is his most mellow work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the calm — the album trades politics for love songs. 'Is This Love' became a global wedding favorite.

name: Survival
teaser: 1979 Bob Marley's political return: 'Zimbabwe', 'So Much Trouble in the World', and 'Africa Unite' are militant anthems of black liberation. The album supported the African liberation movements. It is his most political work since Burnin'.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the message — 'Zimbabwe' became an anthem at the country's independence. The album is a call for unity.

tracks.title: So Much Trouble in the World

name: Uprising
teaser: 1980 Bob Marley's final album: 'Could You Be Loved', 'Redemption Song', and 'Forever Loving Jah' are his most spiritual. The album was released months before his death. 'Redemption Song' is his greatest late song.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Redemption Song' — the acoustic ballad is a meditation on freedom. The album is a profound farewell.

name: Confrontation
teaser: 1983 Bob Marley's posthumous album of outtakes: 'Buffalo Soldier', 'Rastaman Live Up', and 'Blackman Redemption' are raw and powerful. The album was completed by the Wailers after his death. It is a fitting final chapter.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the outtakes — the album captures Marley's final sessions. 'Buffalo Soldier' was written about black soldiers in the US cavalry.

name: The Clash
teaser: 1977 The Clash's debut is punk's most ambitious first statement: 'White Riot', 'London's Burning', and 'Janie Jones' mix reggae, rockabilly, and rage. The album was recorded in three weeks. It remains a landmark of British punk.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the reggae — the band's punk-reggae blend was ahead of its time. 'White Riot' was inspired by a real riot.

tracks.title: I'm So Bored with the USA

name: Give 'Em Enough Rope
teaser: 1978 The Clash's second album, produced by Sandy Pearlman: 'Safe European Home', 'Tommy Gun', and 'English Civil War' are tighter and more professional. The album was criticized by purists. It is a strong bridge to London Calling.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Pearlman gave the album a harder rock sound. 'Safe European Home' is a standout.

tracks.title: Julie's Been Working for the Drug Squad
All the Young Punks (New Boots and Contracts)

name: Sandinista!
teaser: 1980 The Clash's sprawling triple album: 'The Magnificent Seven', 'Police on My Back', and 'The Call Up' span punk, reggae, funk, and gospel. The album was a commercial risk that lost money. It is a fascinating document of ambition.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the range — the album includes hip-hop, dub, and children's songs. It rewards patient listening.

name: Combat Rock
teaser: 1982 The Clash's final album: 'Rock the Casbah', 'Should I Stay or Should I Go', and 'Straight to Hell' are their biggest hits. The album was recorded after internal tensions. It made them stars in America.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the hits — 'Should I Stay or Should I Go' became their biggest US single. 'Straight to Hell' is a dark masterpiece.

tracks.title: Should I Stay or Should I Go
He Who Dares or Is Tired

name: Leave Home
teaser: 1977 The Ramones' second album: 'Pinhead', 'Gimme Gimme Shock Treatment', and 'Suzy Is a Headbanger' are faster and funnier. The album's cover featured a rare group photo. It is the essential Ramones follow-up.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the energy — the album was recorded in two weeks. 'Pinhead' introduced the 'Gabba Gabba Hey' chant.

tracks.title: Oh Oh I Love Her So
Now I Wanna Be a Good Boy
You Should Never Have Opened That Door

name: Rocket to Russia
teaser: 1977 The Ramones' commercial peak: 'Sheena Is a Punk Rocker', 'Rockaway Beach', and 'Teenage Lobotomy' are catchy, fast, and funny. The album was their best-seller. It is considered their greatest work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the melodies — the album's hooks are the catchiest of their career. 'Sheena Is a Punk Rocker' was their first chart hit.

tracks.title: Why Is It Always This Way?

name: Road to Ruin
teaser: 1978 The Ramones' fourth album: 'I Wanna Be Sedated', 'Don't Come Close', and 'She's the One' show the band slowing down and adding ballads. The album was produced by Tommy Ramone. It is their most varied work of the 70s.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'I Wanna Be Sedated' — the song's manic energy made it their signature. The album's ballads showed new depth.

tracks.title: I Just Want to Have Something to Do

name: End of the Century
teaser: 1980 The Ramones' album with producer Phil Spector: 'Do You Remember Rock 'n' Roll Radio?', 'Rock 'n' Roll High School', and 'Baby, I Love You' are glossy and emotional. The sessions with Spector were legendary for their difficulty. It is their strangest album.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Spector's wall of sound clashes with punk energy. 'Do You Remember Rock 'n' Roll Radio?' is a classic.

tracks.title: Do You Remember Rock 'n' Roll Radio?
The Return of Jackie and Judy
I Can't Make It on Time

name: Master of Reality
teaser: 1971 Black Sabbath's third album: 'Sweet Leaf', 'Children of the Grave', and 'Into the Void' are heavier and slower. The album's dropped tunings and sludge created doom metal. It is their most influential record.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the heaviness — Iommi tuned down and the band slowed to a crawl. 'Sweet Leaf' is about cannabis, 'Into the Void' is science fiction.

name: Vol. 4
teaser: 1972 Black Sabbath's fourth album: 'Snowblind', 'Supernaut', and 'Tomorrow's Dream' show the band experimenting with pianos and strings. The album was recorded during their heaviest drug use. It is a peak of their early era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the dynamics — the album swings between crushing riffs and quiet interludes. 'Snowblind' is about cocaine, thinly disguised.

name: Sabbath Bloody Sabbath
teaser: 1973 Black Sabbath's fifth album: 'Sabbath Bloody Sabbath', 'Killing Yourself to Die', and 'A National Acrobat' are their most ambitious. The album was recorded in a haunted castle. It is considered their finest work by many fans.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the arrangements — the album adds synthesizers and orchestral textures. It is the peak of the original lineup.

name: Sabotage
teaser: 1975 Black Sabbath's sixth album: 'Symptom of the Universe', 'Hole in the Sky', and 'Megalomania' are raw and powerful. The album was recorded while the band fought legal battles. It is their last great album of the original era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the aggression — the album is a response to the band's frustrations. 'Symptom of the Universe' is a proto-thrash epic.

name: Heaven and Hell
teaser: 1980 Black Sabbath's comeback with Ronnie James Dio: 'Heaven and Hell', 'Neon Knights', and 'Children of the Sea' are melodic and epic. The album revived the band's career. It is the beginning of the Dio era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the vocals — Dio's operatic voice added a new dimension. The title track is a 7-minute epic.

name: Mob Rules
teaser: 1981 Black Sabbath's second album with Dio: 'The Mob Rules', 'Turn Up the Night', and 'Sign of the Southern Cross' continue the epic style. The album was recorded live in the studio. It is a strong follow-up.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album was recorded in Dallas with a live feel. 'Sign of the Southern Cross' is a highlight.

tracks.title: The Sign of the Southern Cross
Falling Off the Edge of the World

name: Ride the Lightning
teaser: 1984 Metallica's second album: 'Fade to Black', 'For Whom the Bell Tolls', and 'Creeping Death' expand thrash with melody and complexity. The album was recorded in four weeks. It is their creative breakthrough.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the dynamics — the album moves from acoustic passages to thrash attacks. 'Fade to Black' is a haunting ballad.

name: Kill 'Em All
teaser: 1983 Metallica's debut invented thrash metal: 'Seek & Destroy', 'The Four Horsemen', and 'Whiplash' are fast, raw, and relentless. The album was recorded in two weeks. It is the founding document of thrash.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the speed — the album's tempos were unheard of in 1983. 'Seek & Destroy' remains a live staple.

name: Load
teaser: 1996 Metallica's controversial shift: 'Until It Sleeps', 'King Nothing', and 'Hero of the Day' are bluesy, mid-tempo, and commercial. The album's cover art was a controversial mix of fluids. It sold 5 million copies despite fan backlash.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the blues — the album trades thrash for southern-style grooves. It divided fans but aged reasonably well.

name: ReLoad
teaser: 1997 Metallica's companion to Load: 'Fuel', 'The Memory Remains', and 'The Unforgiven II' continue the blues-metal sound. The album was recorded in the same sessions. It is more uneven than its predecessor.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the hits — 'Fuel' is a high-energy opener, 'The Memory Remains' features Marianne Faithfull. The album is a mixed bag.

name: St. Anger
teaser: 2003 Metallica's divisive album: 'St. Anger', 'Frantic', and 'Some Kind of Monster' are raw, loud, and messy. The album was recorded during the band's therapy documented in a film. Its snare drum sound became infamous. It is their most controversial work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the rawness — the album has no guitar solos and a clanging snare. It was a reaction to the band's near-breakup.

name: Death Magnetic
teaser: 2008 Metallica's return to thrash: 'The Day That Never Comes', 'All Nightmare Long', and 'Cyanide' are long, heavy, and fast. The album reunited them with producer Rick Rubin. Its loud mastering drew criticism.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the riffs — the album returns to the complexity of their 80s work. It is their strongest album since the Black Album.

name: Hardwired... to Self-Destruct
teaser: 2016 Metallica's double album: 'Hardwired', 'Moth into Flame', and 'Spit Out the Bone' are aggressive and focused. The album was their first in eight years. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the aggression — the album blends thrash riffs with their classic sound. 'Spit Out the Bone' is a standout.

name: 72 Seasons
teaser: 2023 Metallica's twelfth album: '72 Seasons', 'Lux Aeterna', and 'Screaming Suicide' are long, heavy, and reflective. The album's title refers to the first 18 years of life. It debuted at number two.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the themes — the album meditates on formative years. It is a strong late-career statement.

name: MTV Unplugged in New York
teaser: 1994 Nirvana's acoustic live album: 'The Man Who Sold the World', 'All Apologies', and 'Where Did You Sleep Last Night' are haunting and intimate. The performance was recorded months before Kurt Cobain's death. It is a profound farewell.

exploreAction.targetName: MTV Unplugged in New York (1994) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the cover of Lead Belly's 'Where Did You Sleep Last Night' — the final performance is devastating. The album won a Grammy.

tracks.title: Jesus Doesn't Want Me for a Sunbeam
The Man Who Sold the World
Where Did You Sleep Last Night

name: Bleach
teaser: 1989 Nirvana's debut: 'About a Girl', 'Negative Creep', and 'School' are raw, grungy, and promising. The album was recorded in a month for $600. It is the sound of a band finding its voice.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the raw power — the album is heavier and looser than their later work. 'About a Girl' hints at their melodic side.

name: Facelift
teaser: 1990 Alice in Chains' debut: 'Man in the Box', 'We Die Young', and 'Sea of Sorrow' are heavy, sludgy, and dark. The album's hit single made the band stars. It is the beginning of their signature sound.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the heaviness — the album's riffs are slower and darker than most grunge. 'Man in the Box' is their defining early song.

name: Jar of Flies
teaser: 1994 Alice in Chains' acoustic EP: 'No Excuses', 'I Stay Away', and 'Nutshell' are quiet, haunting, and beautiful. The EP was recorded in a week. It is the first EP to debut at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the harmonies — the EP showcases the band's vocal blend at its most exposed. 'Nutshell' is devastating.

name: Black Gives Way to Blue
teaser: 2009 Alice in Chains' comeback with new singer William DuVall: 'Check My Brain', 'Your Decision', and the title track are heavy and mournful. The title track features Elton John on piano. It is a worthy tribute to Layne Staley.

exploreAction.targetName: Black Gives Way to Blue (2009) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — the piano and vocal duet honor the late Staley. The album marked a successful transition.

name: (What's the Story) Morning Glory?
teaser: 1995 Oasis's masterpiece: 'Wonderwall', 'Don't Look Back in Anger', and 'Champagne Supernova' are the anthems of Britpop. The album sold 22 million copies. It defined mid-90s British rock.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the singalongs — the album is built for stadiums. 'Don't Look Back in Anger' was written by Noel Gallagher in response to 'Wonderwall'.

name: Be Here Now
teaser: 1997 Oasis's bloated third album: 'D'You Know What I Mean?', 'Stand by Me', and 'All Around the World' are overlong and overproduced. The album sold 8 million copies but was criticized for its excess. It is a fascinating failure.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the excess — the album's dense production was a reaction to Britpop's success. 'All Around the World' runs nine minutes.

tracks.title: I Hope, I Think, I Know
The Girl in the Dirty Shirt

name: The Masterplan
teaser: 1998 Oasis's collection of B-sides: 'The Masterplan', 'Acquiesce', and 'Talk Tonight' are as good as their A-sides. The album proved the band's embarrassment of riches. It is a fan favorite.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the quality — the B-sides rival the albums. 'Acquiesce' was voted the band's best song by fans for years.

name: Dig Out Your Soul
teaser: 2008 Oasis's final album: 'The Shock of the Lightning', 'Falling Down', and 'Bag It Up' are loud, psychedelic, and strong. The album was their most experimental since the 90s. It is a fitting finale.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the psychedelia — the album's production embraces noise and electronics. 'The Shock of the Lightning' is a standout.

name: Screamadelica
teaser: 1991 Primal Scream's fusion of rock and dance: 'Loaded', 'Come Together', and 'Higher Than the Sun' blend house beats with psychedelic rock. The album won the first Mercury Prize. It defined the baggy era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the beats — the album was built from dance remixes of their own songs. 'Loaded' samples a Peter Fonda monologue.

tracks.title: Higher than the Sun (A Dub Symphony in Two Parts)
I'm Losing More Than I'll Ever Have

name: Dog Man Star
teaser: 1994 Suede's ambitious second album: 'The Wild Ones', 'We Are the Pigs', and 'Still Life' are grand, orchestral, and cinematic. The album was recorded during the band's breakdown. It is their masterpiece.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the scale — the album's arrangements are lavish and dark. 'Still Life' is an 8-minute orchestral closer.

name: Coming Up
teaser: 1996 Suede's pop rebirth without Bernard Butler: 'Trash', 'Beautiful Ones', and 'Filmstar' are glossy, catchy, and immediate. The album produced five top-ten singles in the UK. It is their most accessible work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the hooks — the album is pure pop-glam. 'Trash' is a statement of intent.

name: Isn't Anything
teaser: 1988 My Bloody Valentine's debut: 'Only Shallow', 'Feed Me with Your Kiss', and 'Soft as Snow' are noisy, dreamy, and revolutionary. The album invented shoegaze. It is the beginning of the genre.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the noise — the album's guitar effects bury the melodies in haze. It is the blueprint for shoegaze.

tracks.title: (When You Wake) You're Still in a Dream
I Can See It (But I Can't Feel It)

name: mbv
teaser: 2013 My Bloody Valentine's return after 22 years: 'She Found Now', 'Only Tomorrow', and 'In Another Way' are immersive and complex. The album was announced on their website at midnight. It is a triumphant comeback.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the evolution — the album's sound is denser than Loveless. 'She Found Now' is a wall of beautiful noise.

name: Pygmalion
teaser: 1995 Slowdive's experimental third album: 'Blue Skied an' Clear', 'Crazy for You', and 'J's Heaven' are minimal, ambient, and strange. The album was a departure that alienated fans. It is now considered ahead of its time.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the restraint — the album strips away guitars for ambient textures. It influenced the post-rock generation.

name: Spiderland
teaser: 1991 Slint's second album invented post-rock: 'Good Morning, Captain', 'Washer', and 'Breadcrumb Trail' are quiet-loud, narrative, and unnerving. The album was recorded in four days. It is one of the most influential albums of the 90s.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the dynamics — the album's whisper-to-scream shifts created a new template. 'Good Morning, Captain' is its climax.

name: Lift Your Skinny Fists Like Antennas to Heaven
teaser: 2000 Godspeed You! Black Emperor's masterpiece: 'Storm', 'Sleep', and 'Static' are 20-minute orchestral-rock epics. The album is built from slow crescendos and field recordings. It is the defining post-rock album.

exploreAction.targetName: Lift Your Skinny Fists Like Antennas to Heaven (2000) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the build — the album's crescendos take 10 minutes to peak. The spoken samples reward attention.

tracks.title: Sleep" * "Murray Ostril: '...They Don't Sleep Anymore on the Beach...'" * "Monheim" * "Broken Windows, Locks of Love Pt. III." / "3rd Part

name: F#A#∞
teaser: 1997 Godspeed You! Black Emperor's debut: 'The Dead Flag Blues', 'East Hastings', and 'Providence' are apocalyptic, cinematic, and bleak. The album's field recordings capture a dying city. It is a statement of despair and beauty.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'The Dead Flag Blues' — its spoken intro is legendary in post-rock. The album is a descent into collapse.

tracks.title: The Dead Flag Blues" * "The Dead Flag Blues (Intro)" * "Slow Moving Trains" / "The Cowboy..." * "The Dead Flag Blues (Outro)

name: Laughing Stock
teaser: 1991 Talk Talk's final album: 'After the Flood', 'Ascension Day', and 'Runeii' are sparse, raw, and transcendent. The album was recorded after their label abandoned them. It is the completion of their transformation.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the rawness — the album sounds like it was recorded in a cathedral. It is a profound final statement.

name: Maxinquaye
teaser: 1995 Tricky's debut is a dark, druggy masterpiece: 'Hell Is Round the Corner', 'Black Steel', and 'Overcome' blend trip-hop, dub, and paranoia. The album's cover recreated a Jimi Hendrix photo with a woman. It is one of the decade's most influential records.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the paranoia — the album's atmosphere is claustrophobic and hypnotic. 'Black Steel' is a Public Enemy cover turned into a dream.

name: Endtroducing.....
teaser: 1996 DJ Shadow's debut is built entirely from samples: 'Midnight in a Perfect World', 'Building Steam with a Grain of Salt', and 'Stem/Long Stem' are cinematic hip-hop instrumentals. The album is in the Guinness Book of Records as the first made entirely from samples. It is a landmark of instrumental hip-hop.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the samples — the album is a collage of obscure records and film dialogue. It rewards headphones and repeated listens.

tracks.title: Building Steam with a Grain of Salt
What Does Your Soul Look Like (Part 4)
What Does Your Soul Look Like (Part 1 – Blue Sky Revisit)" / "Transmission 3

name: Donuts
teaser: 2006 J Dilla's final album: 'Workinonit', 'Time: The Donut of the Heart', and 'Lightworks' are 31 short beats made from samples. The album was recorded in the hospital as Dilla died. It is a testament to his genius.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the brevity — each beat is under two minutes, a burst of genius. The album is the most influential beat tape ever.

tracks.title: Time: The Donut of the Heart

name: Exmilitary
teaser: 2011 Death Grips' mixtape debut: 'Guillotine', 'Takyon', and 'Known for It' are raw, confrontational, and sampled from rock. The album was released free online. It built their cult following.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the samples — the mixtape uses rock and metal samples in rap. 'Guillotine' is their breakout track.

tracks.title: I Want It I Need It (Death Heated)

name: The Powers That B
teaser: 2015 Death Grips' double album: 'On GP', 'Up My Sleeves', and 'Black Quarterback' alternate between Bjork collaborations and industrial rock. The album was released as two discs. 'On GP' is their most personal song.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the range — the album spans noise, rap, and melodic rock. 'On GP' is a confession about family and suicide.

tracks.title: I Break Mirrors with My Face in the United States

name: Bottomless Pit
teaser: 2016 Death Grips' most cohesive album: 'Giving Bad People Good Ideas', 'Bubbles Buried in This Jungle', and 'Eh' are brutal and focused. The album was recorded quickly. It is a strong late entry.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the precision — the album's production is cleaner than their earlier work. 'Giving Bad People Good Ideas' is relentless.

tracks.title: Three Bedrooms in a Good Neighborhood

name: Trouble Man
teaser: 1972 Marvin Gaye's soundtrack for the film about a street hustler: 'Trouble Man', 'T Plays It Cool', and 'Theme from Trouble Man' are jazz-funk instrumentals with spoken interludes. The album was recorded in two weeks. It is a cool, confident detour in his catalog.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the funk — the album's instrumental grooves are among Gaye's most cinematic. The title track became a hit single.

name: How Sweet It Is to Be Loved by You
teaser: 1965 Marvin Gaye's album built around the hit title track: 'How Sweet It Is', 'I'll Be Doggone', and 'Ain't That Peculiar' are upbeat Motown soul. The album showcases his transition from balladeer to hitmaker. It is a strong early collection.

exploreAction.targetName: How Sweet It Is to Be Loved by You (1965) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the hits — the album collects several of Gaye's biggest early singles. The title track was later covered by James Taylor.

name: United
teaser: 1967 Marvin Gaye and Tammi Terrell's duet album: 'Ain't No Mountain High Enough', 'Your Precious Love', and 'If I Could Build My Whole World Around You' are joyful Motown duets. The album made them the label's premier duo. It is a classic of its genre.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the chemistry — Gaye and Terrell's voices blend effortlessly. 'Ain't No Mountain' was later a Diana Ross hit.

name: Moods of Marvin Gaye
teaser: 1966 Marvin Gaye's album of standards and soul: 'One More Heartache', 'Take This Heart of Mine', and 'Little Darling' show his range. The album was part of Motown's push to cross him over. It is a polished mid-60s set.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the standards — the album mixes soul originals with pop covers. It shows Gaye's versatility before his classic era.

tracks.title: You've Been a Long Time Coming
One for My Baby (and One More for the Road)

name: Where I'm Coming From
teaser: 1971 Marvin Gaye's transitional album: 'What's Going On' aside, the album features 'The Chaser', 'Sad Tomorrows', and 'You're the Man'. Gaye co-wrote with his wife Anna Gordy. It is the bridge to his masterpiece.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the songwriting — Gaye was taking control of his material for the first time. The album led directly to What's Going On.

tracks.title: Think of Me as Your Soldier
Take Up a Course in Happiness
Never Dreamed You'd Leave in Summer

name: Up-Tight
teaser: 1966 Stevie Wonder's breakthrough album: 'Uptight (Everything's Alright)', 'Blowin' in the Wind', and 'A Place in the Sun' made him a star at 15. The title track's horn-driven funk was a new sound for Motown. It is his first classic.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the funk — the title track's groove was a departure for Motown. The album established Wonder as more than a child prodigy.

tracks.title: Nothing's Too Good for My Baby

name: I Was Made to Love Her
teaser: 1967 Stevie Wonder's album built on his hit title track: 'I Was Made to Love Her', 'I Love Every Little Thing About You', and 'Until You Come Back to Me' are warm and funky. The title track became one of his signature early songs. It is a strong late-60s set.

exploreAction.targetName: I Was Made to Love Her (1967) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — its groove and Wonder's vocal power made it a classic. The album shows his rapid growth.

name: Journey Through the Secret Life of Plants
teaser: 1979 Stevie Wonder's ambitious soundtrack: 'Send One Your Love', 'The Secret Life of Plants', and 'Venus' Flytrap and the Bug' are orchestral and experimental. The album was written for a nature documentary. It is his most unusual work.

exploreAction.targetName: Journey Through the Secret Life of Plants (1979) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the experimentation — the album uses synthesizers and orchestras in unexpected ways. It is a cult favorite among his fans.

name: Characters
teaser: 1987 Stevie Wonder's album of solo performances: 'Skeletons', 'You Will Know', and 'Free' feature Wonder playing nearly everything. The album won a Grammy for Best Male R&B Vocal. It is his strongest album of the 80s.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the solo performances — Wonder plays most instruments on the album. 'Skeletons' is a funky highlight.

tracks.title: With Each Beat of My Heart
Come Let Me Make Your Love Come Down

name: Various Positions
teaser: 1984 Leonard Cohen's album that almost wasn't released: 'Hallelujah', 'Dance Me to the End of Love', and 'The Night Comes On' are among his greatest songs. The label initially shelved the album. 'Hallelujah' would become one of the most covered songs ever.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Hallelujah' — the song took years to write and became a standard. The album is a late-blooming classic.

tracks.title: Dance Me to the End of Love

name: Old Ideas
teaser: 2012 Leonard Cohen's return after eight years: 'Going Home', 'Amen', and 'Darkness' are warm, witty, and wise. The album's production is spare and intimate. It was a critical and commercial success.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the humor — the album finds Cohen at his most self-aware. 'Going Home' imagines his own legend.

name: Popular Problems
teaser: 2014 Leonard Cohen's album of aging: 'Almost Like the Blues', 'Samson in New Orleans', and 'A Street' are grave and beautiful. The album was written quickly after a burst of creativity. It debuted at number one in Canada.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the gravity — the album addresses mortality with clarity. 'Almost Like the Blues' is a standout.

name: Thanks for the Dance
teaser: 2019 Leonard Cohen's posthumous album: 'Happens to the Heart', 'Moving On', and 'The Goal' were completed by his son and musicians after his death. The album features Beck, Damien Rice, and others. It is a gentle final chapter.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the farewell — the album completes songs Cohen left behind. 'Happens to the Heart' is a wry meditation on aging.

name: His Band and the Street Choir
teaser: 1970 Van Morrison's second album: 'Domino', 'Blue Money', and 'Call Me Up in Dreamland' are loose, joyful, and R&B-driven. The album was recorded live in the studio. It is his most fun record.

exploreAction.targetName: His Band and the Street Choir (1970) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the energy — the album's live-in-studio sound is immediate. 'Domino' became a top-ten hit.

name: Hard Nose the Highway
teaser: 1973 Van Morrison's mixed album: 'Warm Love', 'Hard Nose the Highway', and 'The Great Deception' are ambitious but uneven. The album is known for its beautiful title track and a long suite. It is a transitional work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — its arrangement is among Morrison's loveliest. The album rewards selective listening.

name: No Guru, No Method, No Teacher
teaser: 1986 Van Morrison's spiritual album: 'In the Garden', 'Here Comes the Knight', and 'Thanksgiving' are meditative and devotional. The album is among his most direct statements of faith. It is a fan favorite.

exploreAction.targetName: No Guru, No Method, No Teacher (1986) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the meditation — the album's grooves are long and contemplative. 'In the Garden' is a standout.

name: Poetic Champions Compose
teaser: 1987 Van Morrison's album of romance and jazz: 'Someone Like You', 'Alan Watts Blues', and 'Queen of the Slipstream' are elegant and lyrical. The album's first half is instrumental jazz. It is his smoothest work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the jazz — the album's first side is all instrumentals. 'Someone Like You' became a wedding favorite.

tracks.title: Sometimes I Feel Like a Motherless Child (traditional)

name: Irish Heartbeat
teaser: 1988 Van Morrison's album of Irish songs with the Chieftains: 'Star of the County Down', 'She Moved Through the Fair', and 'Carrickfergus' are traditional and gorgeous. The album celebrates his roots. It is a unique entry in his catalog.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the tradition — the Chieftains' instrumentation transforms the songs. The album is a love letter to Ireland.

tracks.title: Tá Mo Chleamhnas Déanta (My Match It Is Made)

name: Too Long in Exile
teaser: 1993 Van Morrison's album of blues and gospel: 'Too Long in Exile', 'Sweet Thing', and 'Forever Young' feature a big band and guest John Lee Hooker. The album was a return to his blues roots. It is a strong late-period work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the blues — the album is rooted in the genre Morrison grew up on. 'Forever Young' is a duet with John Lee Hooker.

exploreAction.targetName: How Long Has This Been Going On (1995) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the standards — the album showcases Morrison's love of jazz singing. It is a relaxed, late-night record.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the covers — the album honors Hank Williams, Wilson Pickett, and others. It is an affectionate collection.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the joy — the album's songs celebrate music itself. 'Meet Me in the Indian Summer' is a highlight.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album's sound is clean and confident. The title track is a slow-burning classic.

teaser: 2018 Van Morrison's album of jazz and blues: 'The Prophet Speaks', 'Ain't Gonna Moan No More', and 'Love Is a Hard Game' are warm and rootsy. The album features organist Joey DeFrancesco. It is a strong late work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the organ — DeFrancesco's playing anchors the album. It is a soulful, unhurried set.

name: Three Chords and the Truth
teaser: 2019 Van Morrison's album of original songs: 'Dark Night of the Soul', 'Three Chords and the Truth', and 'Every Time I See a River' are classic Morrison. The album's title references his songwriting philosophy. It is a strong statement.

exploreAction.targetName: Three Chords and the Truth (2019) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the songs — the album is built on Morrison's signature blend of soul and reflection. It rewards a full listen.

I Don't Wanna See the Light
I've Got a Tiger By the Tail

name: Babylon by Bus
teaser: 1978 Bob Marley's live double album: 'Exodus', 'Get Up, Stand Up', and 'Jamming' capture the Wailers on their European tour. The album was recorded at the Paris Pavillon and London Rainbow. It is the definitive live Marley record.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the energy — the live versions extend the studio songs with longer grooves. The album is a must for reggae fans.

name: Talkin' Blues
teaser: 1991 Bob Marley's collection of radio sessions and outtakes: 'Talkin' Blues', 'Kaya', and 'Rastaman Chant' capture the Wailers in 1973. The album includes interviews with the band. It is a raw, historical document.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the rawness — the recordings predate the band's studio polish. The interviews add historical context.

name: Soul Rebels
teaser: 1970 The Wailers' album for the Trojan label: 'Soul Rebel', 'Try Me', and 'It's Alright' are raw early reggae. The album was recorded before the band's international breakthrough. It is a fascinating origin point.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the rawness — the album captures the Wailers' early sound. 'Soul Rebel' is a classic of the era.

name: Cut the Crap
teaser: 1985 The Clash's final album: 'This Is England', 'Dictator', and 'Are You Red..Y' were recorded with only Joe Strummer from the original lineup. The album was a commercial and critical failure. It is a cautionary ending to a great band.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the context — the album's dated production obscures some strong Strummer songs. 'This Is England' is a highlight.

name: The Story of the Clash, Vol. 1
teaser: 1988 The Clash's double-disc compilation: 'London Calling', 'Should I Stay or Should I Go', and 'Train in Vain' trace their career. The album includes rarities and B-sides. It is an excellent introduction.

exploreAction.targetName: The Story of the Clash, Vol. 1 (1988) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the range — the compilation spans punk, reggae, and rockabilly. It is the best Clash overview.

tracks.title: Should I Stay or Should I Go
Capital Radio One (preceded by Circle Line interview part 2)

name: Too Tough to Die
teaser: 1984 The Ramones' return to form: 'Howling at the Moon (Sha-La-La)', 'Wart Hog', and 'Endless Nightmare' are fast, raw, and funny. The album was recorded with a new drummer. It is their strongest album of the 80s.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the energy — the album revives the speed of their early records. It is a fan favorite among later Ramones.

name: Animal Boy
teaser: 1986 The Ramones' album produced by Jean Beauvoir: 'Somebody Put Something in My Drink', 'Bonzo Goes to Bitburg', and 'Animal Boy' are political and playful. The album's title track is a highlight. It is a solid mid-80s entry.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the politics — 'Bonzo Goes to Bitburg' criticizes Reagan's visit to a German cemetery. The album is a strong set.

tracks.title: Somebody Put Something in My Drink
My Brain Is Hanging Upside Down (Bonzo Goes to Bitburg)

name: Halfway to Sanity
teaser: 1987 The Ramones' album with new guitarist Richie Ramone: 'I Wanna Live', 'Bop 'Til You Drop', and 'Garden of Serenity' are energetic and varied. The album is a solid late-80s set. It is their last great record of the decade.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the variety — the album mixes fast punk with poppier songs. 'Garden of Serenity' is a highlight.

name: Brain Drain
teaser: 1989 The Ramones' album with the hit 'Pet Sematary': 'Pet Sematary', 'I Believe in Miracles', and 'Zero Zero UFO' are catchy and dark. The album was written with Stephen King's film in mind. It is their most successful late work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the hits — 'Pet Sematary' became their biggest late-career single. The album is a strong farewell to the 80s.

tracks.title: Can't Get You Outta My Mind
Merry Christmas (I Don't Want to Fight Tonight)

name: Mondo Bizarro
teaser: 1992 The Ramones' album after a brief breakup: 'Censorshit', 'Poison Heart', and 'Strength to Endure' are mature and melodic. The album reunited them with producer Ed Stasium. It is a strong comeback.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the maturity — the album's songs address aging and politics. 'Poison Heart' is a standout.

tracks.title: The Job That Ate My Brain

name: Acid Eaters
teaser: 1993 The Ramones' covers album: 'Surf City', 'Somebody to Love', and 'My Back Pages' are punk versions of 60s classics. The album was a tribute to their influences. It is a fun detour.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the covers — the band transforms 60s hits with punk speed. 'Somebody to Love' is a highlight.

tracks.title: Journey to the Center of the Mind
The Shape of Things to Come
Can't Seem to Make You Mine
Have You Ever Seen the Rain?

name: Adios Amigos
teaser: 1995 The Ramones' final album: 'I Don't Want to Grow Up', 'The Crusher', and 'Born to Die in Berlin' are a fitting goodbye. The album's title and cover signal the end. It is a strong finale.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the farewell — the album closes with the band's signature sound. 'I Don't Want to Grow Up' is a Tom Waits cover.

tracks.title: I Don't Want to Grow Up
It's Not for Me to Know

name: It's Alive
teaser: 1979 The Ramones' live album from London: 'Blitzkrieg Bop', 'Sheena Is a Punk Rocker', and 'Rockaway Beach' capture the band at full speed. The album is one of the greatest live punk records. It documents the band's legend.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the speed — the band plays at breakneck pace throughout. The audience reaction is electric.

tracks.title: I Don't Wanna Walk Around With You
Today Your Love, Tomorrow the World
Now I Wanna Be a Good Boy
Oh Oh I Love Her So
Now I Wanna Sniff Some Glue

name: Loco Live
teaser: 1991 The Ramones' second live album: 'The KKK Took My Baby Away', 'Pet Sematary', and 'I Wanna Be Sedated' capture the band in 1991. The album was recorded in Barcelona. It is a raw document of their late era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the energy — the band sounds tight and ferocious. The album is a must for completists.

name: Ramones Mania
teaser: 1988 The Ramones' first compilation: 'Blitzkrieg Bop', 'I Wanna Be Sedated', and 'Rock 'n' Roll High School' trace their first 12 years. The album went gold. It is the essential Ramones collection.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the hits — the compilation collects the band's best-known songs. It is the perfect entry point.

name: Hey Ho! Let's Go: The Anthology
teaser: 1999 The Ramones' double-disc career retrospective: 'Blitzkrieg Bop', 'I Wanna Be Your Boyfriend', and 'Pet Sematary' span the entire catalog. The anthology includes rarities and live cuts. It is the definitive Ramones document.

exploreAction.targetName: Hey Ho! Let's Go: The Anthology (1999) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the arc — the compilation traces the band from 1976 to 1995. It is a fitting tribute to the Ramones.

name: Shut Down Volume 2
teaser: 1964 The Beach Boys' album of car and surf songs: 'Fun, Fun, Fun', 'Don't Worry Baby', and 'The Warmth of the Sun' are among their best early songs. The album captures the car culture of the era. It is a strong early collection.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the ballads — 'Don't Worry Baby' and 'The Warmth of the Sun' show Wilson's emotional depth. The album is a fan favorite.

tracks.title: Why Do Fools Fall in Love

name: Little Deuce Coupe
teaser: 1963 The Beach Boys' album entirely about cars: 'Little Deuce Coupe', 'Custom Machine', and 'Shut Down' are playful and catchy. The album was a commercial hit. It is a novelty executed with charm.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the theme — every song celebrates hot rods. The album is a time capsule of early 60s car culture.

name: Summer Days (And Summer Nights!!)
teaser: 1965 The Beach Boys' album with the classic 'California Girls' on it: 'California Girls', 'Help Me, Rhonda', and 'Let Him Run Wild' are the band at their commercial peak. The album was their biggest seller to date. It is a summery classic.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the harmonies — the album's vocal arrangements are among the band's best. 'California Girls' is an all-time classic.

tracks.title: The Girl from New York City
I'm Bugged at My Ol' Man

name: Beach Boys' Party!
teaser: 1965 The Beach Boys' album of casual recordings: 'Barbara Ann', 'Hang On Sloopy', and 'The Times They Are A-Changin'' are loose, fun, and mostly covers. The album was recorded at a party-like session. 'Barbara Ann' became a surprise hit.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the looseness — the album captures the band relaxing and joking. 'Barbara Ann' is the standout.

tracks.title: You've Got to Hide Your Love Away

name: The Beach Boys Love You
teaser: 1977 The Beach Boys' synth-heavy album: 'Let Us Go on This Way', 'Mona', and 'Love Is a Woman' are quirky, childlike, and personal. The album is Brian Wilson's most direct solo-like statement. It has become a cult favorite.

exploreAction.targetName: The Beach Boys Love You (1977) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the quirk — the album is Wilson's love letter to the Moog synthesizer. It is beloved by fans for its strangeness.

tracks.title: Let Us Go On This Way

name: L.A. (Light Album)
teaser: 1979 The Beach Boys' album of soft rock: 'Good Timin'', 'Angel Come Home', and 'Here Comes the Night' are mellow and polished. The album's disco remake of 'Here Comes the Night' was controversial. It is a transitional work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the ballads — 'Good Timin'' and 'Angel Come Home' are highlights. The disco track divides fans.

name: Keepin' the Summer Alive
teaser: 1980 The Beach Boys' album of sun-soaked pop: 'Keepin' the Summer Alive', 'Oh Darlin'', and 'Some of Your Love' are warm and catchy. The album was recorded with a returning lineup. It is a pleasant late entry.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — its chorus is pure summer. The album is a light, enjoyable set.

tracks.title: School Day (Ring! Ring! Goes the Bell)

name: In the Groove
teaser: 1968 Marvin Gaye's album of the hit 'I Heard It Through the Grapevine': 'I Heard It Through the Grapevine', 'You're What's Happening (In the World Today)', and 'Chained' are among his best late-60s songs. The title track became his biggest hit. It is a career high point.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'I Heard It Through the Grapevine' — its groove and Gaye's vocal made it a Motown landmark. The album is a strong collection.

tracks.title: I Heard It Through the Grapevine
Loving You Is Sweeter Than Ever
You're What's Happening (In The World Today)

name: Someday at Christmas
teaser: 1967 Stevie Wonder's holiday album: 'Someday at Christmas', 'The Little Drummer Boy', and 'What Christmas Means to Me' are warm and joyful. The title track has a social message. It is a beloved seasonal classic.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — its message of peace stands out among holiday songs. The album is a holiday favorite.

tracks.title: A Warm Little Home on a Hill

name: In Concert
teaser: 2003 Van Morrison's live album from his 1979 tour: 'Moondance', 'Cyprus Avenue', and 'And It Stoned Me' are stretched into long jams. The album captures him at his peak. It is a must for fans.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the jams — the live versions extend the studio songs dramatically. The album is a peak live document.

name: Who Built the Moon?
teaser: 2017 Noel Gallagher's High Flying Birds' album produced by David Holmes: 'Holy Mountain', 'She Taught Me How to Fly', and 'Fort Knox' are psychedelic, electronic, and anthemic. The album was a deliberate departure from Oasis-style rock. It debuted at number one in the UK.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Holmes brought a psychedelic edge to Gallagher's songwriting. 'Holy Mountain' is a standout.

tracks.title: She Taught Me How to Fly
Be Careful What You Wish For
The Man Who Built the Moon

name: Council Skies
teaser: 2023 Noel Gallagher's fourth solo album: 'Council Skies', 'Easy Now', and 'Pretty Boy' are warm, melodic, and nostalgic. The album was inspired by his Manchester upbringing. It is his most personal solo work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the melodies — the album is full of Gallagher's trademark hooks. The title track is a highlight.

tracks.title: Open the Door, See What You Find
Trying to Find a World That's Been and Gone: Part 1

name: Second Coming
teaser: 1994 The Stone Roses' long-delayed follow-up: 'Love Spreads', 'Ten Storey Love Song', and 'Begging You' are heavier and more jam-oriented. The album took five years and was a commercial success but critical disappointment. It has been re-evaluated over time.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitar — John Squire's playing dominates the album. 'Love Spreads' is a bluesy epic.

name: Vanishing Point
teaser: 1997 Primal Scream's return to rock: 'Kowalski', 'Star', and 'Burning Wheel' are motorik, propulsive, and cinematic. The album was inspired by the 1971 film of the same name. It is their most focused work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the drive — the album's motorik rhythms never let up. 'Kowalski' is a standout.

name: Head Music
teaser: 1999 Suede's electronic album: 'Electricity', 'Can't Get Enough', and 'Everything Will Flow' blend their glam rock with dance production. The album was a commercial success but divided fans. It is their most synth-heavy work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album embraces 90s electronic sounds. 'Electricity' is a dance-rock hybrid.

name: A New Morning
teaser: 2002 Suede's subdued album: 'Positivity', 'Obsessions', and 'Lost in TV' are gentler and more acoustic. The album was a commercial disappointment. It is their most understated work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the restraint — the album trades glam for introspection. 'Positivity' is a highlight.

tracks.title: One Hit to the Body (Tony Hoffer Version)
When the Rain Falls (Tony Hoffer Version)

name: Bloodsports
teaser: 2013 Suede's reunion album: 'Barriers', 'It Starts and Ends with You', and 'Hit Me' are urgent, glammy, and strong. The album marked their return after a decade. It was a critical success.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the energy — the album recaptures the band's early drama. 'Barriers' is a standout.

tracks.title: It Starts and Ends with You
Sometimes I Feel I'll Float Away
What Are You Not Telling Me?

name: Night Thoughts
teaser: 2016 Suede's cinematic album: 'Outsiders', 'No Tomorrow', and 'Like Kids' are grand and dark. The album was accompanied by a feature film. It is their most ambitious reunion work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the scale — the album's songs are built for drama. The companion film adds a new dimension.

tracks.title: I Don't Know How to Reach You
What I'm Trying to Tell You
I Can't Give Her What She Wants

name: The Blue Hour
teaser: 2018 Suede's concept album about childhood: 'Wastelands', 'Life Is Golden', and 'The Invisibles' are atmospheric and strange. The album features children's choir and spoken word. It is their most experimental work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the atmosphere — the album's production is eerie and beautiful. 'Life Is Golden' is a highlight.

tracks.title: Don't Be Afraid If Nobody Loves You

name: Autofiction
teaser: 2022 Suede's raw, direct album: 'She Still Leads Me On', '15 Again', and 'It's Always the Quiet Ones' are the band at their most immediate. The album was recorded live in the studio. It is their best reunion work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the rawness — the album was cut live with minimal overdubs. 'She Still Leads Me On' is a highlight.

tracks.title: The Only Way I Can Love You
Turn Off Your Brain and Yell
The Sadness in You, The Sadness in Me
There Is No Me If There Is No You

name: Just for a Day
teaser: 1991 Slowdive's debut: 'Spanish Air', 'Catch the Breeze', and 'Avalyn' are dreamy, droning, and gorgeous. The album was released in the shoegaze boom. It is a strong foundation for their later work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the haze — the album's guitars wash over the melodies. 'Catch the Breeze' is a standout.

name: Slowdive
teaser: 2017 Slowdive's reunion album after 22 years: 'Star Roving', 'Sugar for the Pill', and 'Slomo' are lush, warm, and confident. The album was a critical and commercial success. It is a triumphant return.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the warmth — the album's production is richer than their 90s work. 'Slomo' is a standout.

name: everything is alive
teaser: 2023 Slowdive's fifth album: 'shanty', 'alife', and 'kisses' are dreamy, electronic, and hopeful. The album was recorded with producer Sune Rose Wagner. It is their most electronic work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the textures — the album blends guitars with electronic beats. 'shanty' is a highlight.

name: Yanqui U.X.O.
teaser: 2002 Godspeed You! Black Emperor's third album: '09-15-00', 'Rockets Fall on Rocket Falls', and 'Motherfucker=Redemption' are long, orchestral, and political. The album was recorded with a full orchestra. It is their most ambitious work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the orchestra — the album's arrangements are the band's grandest. It rewards patient listening.

tracks.title: Motherfucker=Redeemer (cont.) * (Hidden track: George Bush Cut Up While Talking)

name: The Colour of Spring
teaser: 1986 Talk Talk's transitional album: 'Life's What You Make It', 'Living in Another World', and 'Happiness Is Easy' blend their pop past with their experimental future. The album was a hit. It is the bridge to their masterpieces.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the transition — the album moves from synth-pop toward organic arrangements. 'Life's What You Make It' is a classic.

name: Psyence Fiction
teaser: 1998 UNKLE's debut, produced by DJ Shadow: 'Rabbit in Your Headlights', 'Be There', and 'Lonely Soul' feature guests like Thom Yorke and Richard Ashcroft. The album was a landmark of trip-hop. It is a cinematic, star-studded record.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guests — Thom Yorke, Richard Ashcroft, and Mike D appear. 'Rabbit in Your Headlights' is a standout.
